  60class BrachyDose:
  61    r"""
  62    Purpse: 
  63        This class holds information regarding a dose distribution as well as the fundamental 
  64    functions that are applied on the dose. All the doses are J/Gy. 
  65
  66    Attributes:
  67        grid:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose at each voxel. [z, y, x]
  68        uncertainty:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose uncertainity at each voxel. [z, y, x] 
  69        num_voxels:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the number of grid points on x, y, z axis. 
  70        voxel_size:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the resolution of each voxel along x, y, z axis in centimeters. 
  71        origin_coordinates:np.ndarray := The spatial coordinate of the "bottom" left corner of the image in centrimeters. [x, y, z] 
  72        voxel_edges:np.ndarray := coorindates of voxel edges along z, y and x axis.  
  73

 133    def load_file_to_brachydose(self, pth_dose_file: str):
 134        r""" 
 135        Purpose: 
 136        given the path to a file holding dose information, it will return 
 137        a BrachyDose object with the populated available attributes. It will give a warning
 138        for the missing attributes.
 139
 140        Inputs:
 141            - pth_dose_file := path directory where the file containing the dose is. The file 
 142                extension could be ".3ddose", ".nrrd", ".dcm", or ".minidos"
 143
 144        Output:
 145        self : BrachyDose
 146        """
 147        pth_dose_file = os.path.abspath(pth_dose_file)
 148
 149        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
 150
 151        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
 152            self.load_from_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
 153        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
 154            self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
 155        elif file_extension == ".dcm":
 156            assert "RD" in pth_dose_file, "must be a dicom dose file starting with 'RD'"
 157            raise NotImplementedError(
 158                "loading dose from dicom is not currently supported")
 159        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
 160            raise NotImplementedError(
 161                "loading dose from .minidos file is not currently supported")
 162        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
 163            raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
 164        else:
 165            raise ValueError("file extension not recognized")
 166        #voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
 167        # print(len(self.voxel_edges))
 168        if(self.interpolation_function is None and self.grid is not None):
 169            self.create_interpolation_function()
 170        return self

 172    def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: str):
 173        r"""
 174        Purpose:
 175        To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically
 176        detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function. 
 177
 178        Inputs:
 179            - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options 
 180            for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd". 
 181
 182        Output:
 183            - void := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"
 184        """
 185        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
 186
 187        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
 188            self.write_to_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
 189
 190        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
 191            self.write_to_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
 192
 193        elif file_extension == ".npz":
 194            self.write_to_npz(pth_dose_file)
 195
 196        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
 197            self.write_to_minidos(pth_dose_file)
 198
 199        elif file_extension == ".xz":
 200            self.write_to_xz(pth_dose_file)
 201
 202        elif file_extension == ".zstd":
 203            self.write_to_zstd(pth_dose_file)
 204
 205        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
 206           raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
 207
 208        else:
 209            raise ValueError(f"The input file name {pth_dose_file} is not supported. the supported \
 210            file types are '.3ddose', '.nrrd', '.npz', '.minidos', '.xz', and '.zstd'")
 211
 212    def load_from_3ddose(self, filename: str):
 213        r""" 
 214        Purpose: 
 215            Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
 216
 217        Input:
 218            - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file
 219        """
 220        assert os.path.splitext(
 221            filename)[-1] == ".3ddose", "this file should have '3ddose' extension."
 222        path = filename
 223        # print("Opening 3ddose at %s" % path)
 224        with open(path, "rb") as newfile:
 225            bench_voxels = [int(i) for i in newfile.readline().split()]
 226            bench_x_pos = np.round(
 227                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
 228            bench_y_pos = np.round(
 229                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
 230            bench_z_pos = np.round(
 231                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
 232
 233            bench_x_spacing = bench_x_pos[1] - bench_x_pos[0]
 234            bench_y_spacing = bench_y_pos[1] - bench_y_pos[0]
 235            bench_slice_thick = bench_z_pos[1] - bench_z_pos[0]
 236
 237            bench_dict = {}
 238
 239            huge_dose_array = np.array(
 240                newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
 241            bench_dose = reshape(
 242                huge_dose_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
 243            try:
 244                huge_uncert_array = np.array(
 245                    newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
 246                bench_uncert = reshape(
 247                    huge_uncert_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
 248                self.uncertainty = bench_uncert
 249            except:
 250                print("Warning: No uncertainty in the 3ddose files")
 251
 252            self.grid = bench_dose
 253            self.num_voxels = np.array(bench_voxels, dtype=np.float32)
 254            self.voxel_size = np.round(np.array(
 255                [bench_x_spacing, bench_y_spacing, bench_slice_thick], dtype=np.float32), 1)
 256            self.origin_coordinates = np.array(
 257                [bench_x_pos[0], bench_y_pos[0], bench_z_pos[0]], dtype=np.float32)
 258            # overriding axis calculation to ignore the axis contents of 3ddose and use the function below
 259            # np.array([bench_z_pos, bench_y_pos, bench_x_pos], dtype=object)
 260            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
 261
 262    def load_from_nrrd(self, pth_nrrd: str):
 263        r"""
 264        Purpose: 
 265            given the path to a nrrd dose file, it will load its content into self:BrachyDose
 266
 267        Inputs: 
 268            - pth_nrrd := Path to a nrrd file writtern by self.to_nrrd()
 269
 270        Dependencies:
 271            - SimpleITK
 272            - calculate_voxel_edges()
 273        """
 274        loaded_image_nrrd = sitk.ReadImage(pth_nrrd, imageIO='NrrdImageIO')
 275        [dose_array, uncertainty_array] = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(
 276            loaded_image_nrrd)
 277        dose_array = np.swapaxes(dose_array, 0, 2)
 278        uncertainty_array = np.swapaxes(uncertainty_array, 0, 2)
 279
 280        self.uncertainty = uncertainty_array.astype(np.float32)
 281        self.grid = dose_array.astype(np.float32)
 282        self.num_voxels = np.array(
 283            np.flip((dose_array.shape), axis=0)).astype(np.float32)
 284        self.voxel_size = np.round(np.array(loaded_image_nrrd.GetSpacing()[
 285                                 1:]).astype(np.float32), 1)
 286        self.origin_coordinates = np.array(loaded_image_nrrd.GetOrigin()[
 287                                1:]).astype(np.float32)
 288        self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
 289

 347    def create_interpolation_function(self):
 348        voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
 349        self.interpolation_function = RegularGridInterpolator(
 350            (voxel_centers[0], voxel_centers[1], voxel_centers[2]), self.grid, bounds_error=False, fill_value = 0)
 351
 352    def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z):
 353        r"""
 354        """
 355        self.is_not_empty()
 356        if (self.interpolation_function is None):
 357            raise ValueError("interpolation function is not defined")
 358        shape = []
 359        axis = []
 360        for coord in [z, y, x]:
 361            if isinstance(coord, float):
 362                coord_size = 1
 363                axis.append([coord])
 364            elif isinstance(coord, np.ndarray):
 365                coord_size = coord.size
 366                axis.append(coord)
 367            else:
 368                raise TypeError(
 369                    "x, y, and z should be either floats or numpy arrays")
 370            shape.append(coord_size)
 371        coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x = np.meshgrid(
 372            [z], [y], [x], indexing='ij')
 373        # print(coord_grid.shape())
 374        dose_grid = self.interpolation_function(
 375            (coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x))
 376        dose_grid.reshape(shape)
 377        return dose_grid.squeeze()
 378
 379    def extract_profile_2d(self, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str):
 380        if not isinstance(axis_1_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(axis_2_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(plane_coord, float):
 381            raise TypeError(
 382                "axis_1_coords and axis_2_coords should be numpy arrays and plane_coord should be a float")
 383        if plane == 'xy':
 384            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord)
 385        elif plane == 'xz':
 386            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, plane_coord, axis_2_coords)
 387        elif plane == 'yz':
 388            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords)
 389        elif plane == 'yx':
 390            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, plane_coord)
 391        elif plane == 'zx':
 392            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, plane_coord, axis_1_coords)
 393        elif plane == 'zy':
 394            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords)
 395        else:
 396            raise ValueError(
 397                "plane should be one of the following: 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', 'yx', 'zx', 'zy'")

 399    def extract_profile_1d(self, axis: str, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, axis_3_coords: List[float]) -> np.ndarray:
 400        r"""
 401        Extracts a 1D line profile from the dose grid along the specified axis, given the coordinates of the other two axes and a list of coordinates along the axis of extraction.
 402
 403        Parameters:
 404            - axis (str): the axis along which to extract the line profile. Must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.
 405            - axis_1_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the first axis, as a 1D numpy array.
 406            - axis_2_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the second axis, as a 1D numpy array.
 407            - axis_3_coords (List[float]): the coordinates along the axis of extraction, as a list of floats.
 408
 409        Returns:
 410            - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.
 411        """
 412        if axis not in ['x', 'y', 'z']:
 413            raise ValueError("axis must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'")
 414
 415        if axis == 'x':
 416            x = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 417            y, z = np.meshgrid(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, indexing='ij')
 418        elif axis == 'y':
 419            y = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 420            x, z = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
 421        else:
 422            z = np.array(axis_3_coords)
 423            x, y = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
 424
 425        dose_grid = self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(x, y, z)
 426        profile = np.mean(dose_grid, axis=(1, 2))
 427        return profile

 433    def get_average_uncert(self) -> float:
 434        r"""
 435        Purpose:
 436            Documentation is missing
 437        """
 438        max_dose = self.grid.max()
 439        dose_mask = self.grid < 0.2 * max_dose
 440        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.uncert, mask=dose_mask)
 441        masked_dose = ma.array(self.grid, mask=dose_mask)
 442        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert / masked_dose) * 100
 443        return average_uncert
 444
 445    def get_average_uncert_benchmark(self) -> float:
 446        r"""
 447        Purpose:
 448            Documentation is missing
 449        """
 450        max_dose = self.grid.max()
 451        dose_mask = self.grid < 0.2 * max_dose
 452        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.uncert, mask=dose_mask)
 453        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert) * 100
 454        return average_uncert

 456    def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_top_left: list):
 457        r''' a function to padd the grid and uncertainty in BrachyDose object and bring it to the desired dimensios.
 458        it will update all the aspects of the dose object to match the new dimensiosn.
 459        The voxels must have the same size! remember, python does z, y, x. 
 460        inputs:
 461            self:BrachyDose
 462
 463            new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:
 464                [new_z_dim, new_y_dim, new_x_dim]
 465
 466            new_top_left := coordinates of the new origin_coordinates
 467                [x, y, z]
 468        '''
 469        assert any(
 470            new_dims > self.grid.shape), "since you are padding, the new dimensions should be larger than the input dimensions"
 471
 472        # calculate distances between the new and old origin_coordinates voxels.
 473        # if for an axis, the distance of origin_coordinatess is larger than the voxel size, use the new origin_coordinates
 474        # else, use the old top left
 475        origin_coordinates_distance = np.abs(new_top_left - self.origin_coordinates)
 476        final_origin_coordinates = np.zeros(3)
 477        for i, distance in zip(range(3), origin_coordinates_distance):
 478            final_origin_coordinates[i] = new_top_left[i] if distance > self.voxel_size[i] else self.origin_coordinates[i]
 479
 480        # figure out how much padding to do before and after each axis
 481        padding = np.zeros([3, 2])
 482        for i in range(3):
 483            if final_origin_coordinates[i] == self.origin_coordinates[i]:
 484                # all padding goes to the end for this dose axis
 485                pad_before = 0
 486                pad_after = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
 487            else:
 488                # all padding goes to the begining of the dose axis
 489                pad_before = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
 490                pad_after = 0
 491            padding[2-i] = [pad_before, pad_after]
 492
 493        # pad the old dose grid to get the new grid!
 494        new_dose_grid = np.pad(self.grid, tuple(
 495            padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
 496        if self.uncertainty is not None:
 497            new_uncert = np.pad(self.uncertainty, tuple(
 498                padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
 499
 500        # figure out the end coordinates based on the padding
 501        # self.voxel_size is a list of x, y and z spacing, we want it to be
 502        # a numpy array of z, y, x spacings.
 503        voxel_size = np.array(self.voxel_size)[:, np.newaxis][::-1]
 504        end_coords_distances = padding * \
 505            np.array([[-1, 1], [-1, 1], [-1, 1]]) * voxel_size
 506
 507        old_end_coords = np.array(
 508            [[self.voxel_edges[0][0], self.voxel_edges[0][-1]],
 509             [self.voxel_edges[1][0], self.voxel_edges[1][-1]],
 510             [self.voxel_edges[2][0], self.voxel_edges[2][-1]]])
 511
 512        new_end_coords = old_end_coords + end_coords_distances
 513
 514        # now padd the new axis with respect to the appropriate begin and end coordinates
 515        new_axis = np.array([np.zeros(new_dims[0]), np.zeros(
 516            new_dims[1]), np.zeros(new_dims[2])], dtype=object)
 517
 518        # pad the new axis with linear ramp
 519        for i in range(new_axis.shape[0]):
 520            new_axis[i] = np.pad(self.voxel_edges[i], tuple(padding[i].astype(
 521                int)), mode='linear_ramp', end_values=new_end_coords[i])
 522
 523        # fillout the new padded dose dictionary
 524        padded_dose = BrachyDose()
 525
 526        padded_dose.grid = new_dose_grid
 527        padded_dose.uncert = new_uncert if self.uncertainty is not None else None
 528        # voxel size remains unchanged
 529        padded_dose.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
 530        padded_dose.origin_coordinates = final_origin_coordinates
 531        padded_dose.voxel_edges = new_axis
 532
 533        return padded_dose
 534
 535    def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str):
 536        r''' 
 537        Purpose: 
 538            This function will write the contents of a BrachyDose onto a text file with .3ddose extension. 
 539
 540        inputs:
 541            - self := a BrachyDose object containing the following keys:
 542                grid [z, y, x]
 543                uncert [z, y, x] 
 544                voxel_size [x, y, z]
 545                origin_coordinates [x, y, z]
 546                axis [z, y, x]
 547
 548            - file_name := the directory path where the file will be written
 549        '''
 550        file_name = os.path.abspath(file_name)
 551
 552        dimensions = ' '.join(map(str, self.num_voxels.astype(int))) + '\n'
 553        x_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[2])) + '\n'
 554        y_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[1])) + '\n'
 555        z_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[0])) + '\n'
 556        dose_flattened = ' '.join(map(str, self.grid.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
 557        if self.uncertainty is not None:
 558            uncertainty_flattened = ' '.join(
 559                map(str, self.uncertainty.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
 560        else:
 561            uncertainty_flattened = ''
 562
 563        with open(file_name, 'w') as file:
 564            lines = [dimensions, x_axis, y_axis, z_axis,
 565                     dose_flattened, uncertainty_flattened]
 566            file.writelines(lines)
 567
 568    def write_to_nrrd(self, file_name: str, metadata: Optional[dict] = None):
 569        r"""
 570            Purpose: 
 571                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file. 
 572            inputs:
 573                - file_name := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to. 
 574
 575                - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later):
 576                    "cancer site": 
 577                    "care center": 
 578                    "number of dwell positions": 
 579                    "number of segmented structures": 
 580                    "patient number": 
 581                    "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]"
 582            outputs: Void
 583                writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd
 584                note that 3D dose files are written in z, y, x, but the sitk image is written in x, y, z. 
 585        """
 586        # create sitk dose image
 587        dose_nda = np.swapaxes(self.grid, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
 588        uncertainty_nda = np.swapaxes(
 589            self.uncertainty, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
 590
 591        image_nrrd = sitk.JoinSeries(
 592            sitk.GetImageFromArray(dose_nda),
 593            sitk.GetImageFromArray(uncertainty_nda)
 594        )
 595        image_nrrd.SetOrigin(np.append([0], self.origin_coordinates))
 596        image_nrrd.SetSpacing(np.append([1], self.voxel_size))
 597
 598        # set the metadata: all sitk Images belonging to a patient will have the same meta data
 599        if metadata is not None:
 600            for key in metadata:
 601                image_nrrd.SetMetaData(key, metadata[key])
 602
 603        # write out the files
 604        file_name_ospth = os.path.abspath(file_name)
 605        assert os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(
 606            file_name_ospth)), f"the input folder does not exist: {os.path.dirname(file_name_ospth)}"
 607
 608        run_number = file_name_ospth.split(".")[0]
 609
 610        sitk.WriteImage(image_nrrd, run_number+".nrrd",
 611                        useCompression=True, compressionLevel=9)
 612
 613    def write_to_npz(self, file_name: str):
 614        r"""
 615            Purpose: 
 616                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a npz file, which is numpy compressed. 
 617
 618            inputs:
 619                - self := BrachyDose object
 620                - file_name := path where the dose npz file will be written to. 
 621
 622            outputs: Void
 623                writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name. 
 624        """
 625
 626        assert os.path.splitext(file_name)[-1] == ".npz"
 627
 628        np.savez_compressed(
 629            file=file_name,
 630            grid=self.grid,
 631            uncertainty=self.uncertainty,
 632            num_voxels=self.num_voxels,
 633            voxel_size=self.voxel_size,
 634            origin_coordinates=self.origin_coordinates,
 635            axis=self.voxel_edges,
 636        )
 637
 638    def write_to_minidos(self, file_name, compress_program: Optional[str] = None):
 639        r"""
 640            Purpose: 
 641                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a minidos file, which is just a binary file written line by line. 
 642                This code is based on Maude Robitaille's implementation. 
 643                This script was developed by Maude Robitaille. 
 644            inputs:
 645                - self := BrachyDose object
 646                - file_name := path where the dose minidos file will be written to. 
 647
 648            outputs: Void
 649                writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name. 
 650        """
 651        assert os.path.splitext(
 652            file_name)[-1] == ".minidos", f"the file name {file_name} should have '.minidos' extension."
 653        with open(file_name, 'wb') as newfile:
 654
 655            # the first line is the number of voxels along each dimension [x, y , z]
 656            dims_array = array('i', self.num_voxels)
 657            dims_array.tofile(newfile)
 658
 659            # lines 2,3 and 4 are the voxel sizes x, y, z
 660            float_array_x = array('f', [self.voxel_size[0]])
 661            float_array_x.tofile(newfile)
 662            float_array_y = array('f', [self.voxel_size[1]])
 663            float_array_y.tofile(newfile)
 664            float_array_z = array('f', [self.voxel_size[2]])
 665            float_array_z.tofile(newfile)
 666
 667            # lines 5, 6, 7 are the origins x, y, and z
 668            originx_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[0]])
 669            originy_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[1]])
 670            originz_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[2]])
 671
 672            originx_array.tofile(newfile)
 673            originy_array.tofile(newfile)
 674            originz_array.tofile(newfile)
 675
 676            # lines 8 is just a zero
 677            zero = array('i', [0])
 678            zero.tofile(newfile)
 679
 680            # line 9-infinit is the dose per voxel array
 681            for d in self.grid.flatten():
 682                array('f', [d]).tofile(newfile)
 683
 684    def write_to_xz(self, fileName):
 685        assert os.path.splitext(fileName)[-1] == '.xz'
 686
 687        with lzma.open(fileName, 'wb') as file:
 688            pickle.dump(self, file)

 696    def calculate_voxel_edges(self):
 697        r"""
 698        Purpose: will calculate the axies coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary.
 699        Input: 
 700            - dose := output of load_3ddose(). it should have the following keys and values:
 701                {"grid":,
 702                "origin_coordinates":,
 703                "voxel_size":}
 704        Output: 
 705            - axes:numpy.array() := 
 706            [[z_min:voxel_size:z_max],
 707            [y_min:voxel_size:y_max],
 708            [x_min:voxel_size:x_max]] 
 709        """
 710        # calculate the end point of axis in 3D space
 711        axes_end = np.array(
 712            # one voxel size is added because np.arange stops at an index before the end
 713            self.origin_coordinates + self.num_voxels * self.voxel_size + self.voxel_size
 714        )
 715                
 716        self.voxel_edges = np.empty(len(axes_end), dtype=object)
 717        for i in range(len(axes_end)):
 718            self.voxel_edges[i] = np.arange(
 719                self.origin_coordinates[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
 720                axes_end[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
 721                self.voxel_size[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
 722                dtype=np.float32)
 723            if np.absolute(self.grid.shape[i] - self.voxel_edges[i].shape[0]) > 1:
 724                self.voxel_edges[i] = self.voxel_edges[i][:-1] 
 725
 726        return self.voxel_edges
 727
 728    def get_voxel_centers(self):
 729        voxel_centers = np.empty(len(self.voxel_edges), dtype=object)
 730        if self.voxel_edges is not None:
 731            for i in range(len(self.voxel_edges)):
 732                voxel_centers[i] = self.voxel_edges[i] + self.voxel_size[i]/2.
 733                voxel_centers[i] = voxel_centers[i][:-1]
 734        else:
 735            raise ValueError("Voxel edges are not calculated yet")
 736        return voxel_centers
 737
 738    def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose):
 739        r"""
 740        Purpose:
 741            To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose
 742
 743        Inputs:
 744            - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain equal info as the attributes of self. 
 745
 746        Outputs:
 747            True if attributes of new_brachy_dose are the same as self
 748            False otherwise
 749        """
 750        assert isinstance(
 751            new_brachy_dose, BrachyDose), "input must be of type BrachyDose"
 752        assert np.array_equal(
 753            self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid), "dose grid is not the same"
 754        assert np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(
 755            new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)), "axis is not the same"
 756        assert np.array_equal(
 757            self.uncertainty, new_brachy_dose.uncertainty), "uncertainty is not the same"
 758        assert np.array_equal(
 759            self.num_voxels, new_brachy_dose.num_voxels), "num_voxels is not the same"
 760        assert np.array_equal(
 761            self.voxel_size, new_brachy_dose.voxel_size), "voxel_size is not the same"
 762        assert np.array_equal(
 763            self.origin_coordinates, new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), "origin_coordinates is not the same"
 764        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)), "voxel_size is not the same"
 765        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2), "origin_coordinates is not the same"
 766
 767        return np.array_equal(self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid) \
 768            and np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)) \
 769            and np.array_equal(self.uncertainty, new_brachy_dose.uncertainty) \
 770            and np.array_equal(self.num_voxels, new_brachy_dose.num_voxels) \
 771            and np.array_equal(self.voxel_size, new_brachy_dose.voxel_size) \
 772            and np.array_equal(self.origin_coordinates, new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates)
 773        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)) \
 774        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2)
 775        # np.array_equal(np.round(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), 2), np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)) \
 776
 777    def crop_by_coordinates(self, coord_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
 778        r"""
 779        Purpose: 
 780            given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
 781            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
 782        Inputs:
 783            - self: BrachyDose object
 784            - coord_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
 785                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
 786        Output:
 787            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
 788                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
 789        Dependencies:
 790            -self.crop_by_index()
 791        """
 792        self.is_not_empty()
 793
 794        # make sure the ending coordinate of the new range is larger than its origin
 795        for ax in coord_range:
 796            assert ax[1] > ax[0], "axis ending coordinate should be larger than its begining coordinate"
 797
 798        # assert coordinate range falls into the image
 799        axes_name = ["x axis(2)", "y axis(1)", "z axis(0)"]
 800        coords_flipped = np.flip(coord_range, 0)
 801        for i in range(self.voxel_edges.shape[0]):
 802            assert coords_flipped[i][0] > self.voxel_edges[i][
 803                0], f"cropping lower limit must be larger than the lowest coordinate on {axes_name[i]}"
 804
 805        # convert new coordinates to indicies for both beggingn and ending (may not be exact)
 806        new_origin_distance = coord_range[:, 0] - self.origin_coordinates
 807
 808        new_origin_index = np.floor(
 809            new_origin_distance / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
 810
 811        new_ending_index = np.floor(
 812            (coord_range[:, 1] - self.origin_coordinates) / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
 813
 814        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
 815
 816        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)
 817
 818    def crop_by_fraction(self, crop_fraction, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
 819        r"""
 820        Purpose: 
 821            given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)*dimension voxels
 822                from the edges of the x and y axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
 823        Inputs:
 824            - self: BrachyDose object
 825            - crop_fraction := a floating point between 0 and 1, which is the fraction of the image axis that remains in the crop. 
 826                for example, a crop ratio of 0.5 will keep the center of the x and y axis, plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. 
 827                The z axis will not be cropped. 
 828                    +++++++++       ---------
 829                    +++++++++       --+++++--
 830                    +++++++++  ===> --+++++--
 831                    +++++++++       --+++++--
 832                    +++++++++       ---------
 833        Output:
 834            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
 835                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
 836        Dependencies:
 837            -self.crop_by_index()
 838        """
 839        assert crop_fraction >= 0 and crop_fraction <= 1, "the fraction should be between 0 and 1"
 840        off_set = 0.5 * (1-crop_fraction)*self.num_voxels
 841        new_origin_index = np.array([off_set[0], off_set[1], 0]).astype(int)
 842        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
 843                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
 844
 845        new_ending_index = np.array(
 846            [self.num_voxels[0]-off_set[0], self.num_voxels[1]-off_set[1], self.num_voxels[2]]).astype(int)
 847        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
 848                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
 849
 850        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
 851
 852        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)
 853
 854    def crop_by_index(self, index_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
 855        r"""
 856        Purpose: 
 857            given a range of indicies (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
 858            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
 859        Inputs:
 860            - self: BrachyDose object
 861            - index_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
 862                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
 863        Output:
 864            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the index range. 
 865                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
 866        Dependencies:
 867            - None
 868        """
 869        new_origin_index = index_range[:, 0].astype(int)
 870        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
 871                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
 872
 873        new_ending_index = index_range[:, 1].astype(int)
 874        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
 875                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
 876
 877        # update the attributes
 878        if inplace:
 879            self.grid = self.grid[
 880                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
 881                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
 882                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
 883            ]
 884            self.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
 885                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
 886                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
 887                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
 888            ]
 889            self.origin_coordinates = np.array([
 890                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
 891                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
 892                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
 893            ])
 894            self.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
 895            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
 896        else:
 897            new_dose_obj = BrachyDose()
 898            new_dose_obj.grid = self.grid[
 899                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
 900                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
 901                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
 902            ]
 903            new_dose_obj.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
 904                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
 905                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
 906                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
 907            ]
 908            new_dose_obj.origin_coordinates = np.array([
 909                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
 910                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
 911                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
 912            ])
 913            new_dose_obj.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
 914            new_dose_obj.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
 915            new_dose_obj.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
 916            return new_dose_obj
 917
 918    def is_not_empty(self):
 919        assert self.grid is not None, "error grid is None"
 920        # commenting out the following line, since uncertainty is not always available
 921        # e.g. for gamma and percent difference
 922        # assert self.uncertainty is not None, "error uncertainty is None"
 923        assert self.num_voxels is not None, "error num_voxels is None"
 924        assert self.voxel_size is not None, "error voxel_size is None"
 925        assert self.origin_coordinates is not None, "error origin_coordinates is None"
 926        assert self.voxel_edges is not None, "error axis is None"
 927        return True
 928
 929    def info(self):
 930        self.is_not_empty()
 931        print(f"shape of dose grid is: {self.grid.shape}")
 932        print(f"shape of uncertainty matrix is: {self.uncertainty.shape}")
 933        print(f"num voxels attribute is: {self.num_voxels}")
 934        print(f"the top left (bottom left in reality) is {self.origin_coordinates}")
 935        print(f"the voxel size is {self.voxel_size}")

 938        print(
 939            f"the range of the z axis is {self.voxel_edges[0][0], self.voxel_edges[0][-1]}")
 940        print(
 941            f"the range of the y axis is {self.voxel_edges[1][0], self.voxel_edges[1][-1]}")
 942        print(
 943            f"the range of the x axis is {self.voxel_edges[2][0], self.voxel_edges[2][-1]}")

 945    def crop_by_body_contour(self, body_index_range: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
 946                             body_mask_shape: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
 947                             pth_dir_dicom: Optional[str] = None, ):
 948        r"""
 949        Purpose: 
 950            based on the given dicom structure file, crop the BrachyDose object such 
 951                that it only has the body contour. 
 952        Inputs: 
 953            - pth_dir_dicom := pth_dir_dicom := path to the directory with the dicom files of a patient. 
 954                it should contain both images and RTSTRUCT file. this input is optional
 955
 956            - body_index_range:np.array :=  a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
 957                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]],
 958
 959            - original_mask_dimensions:np.array := 1 x 3 array holding the dimension of the original mask
 960
 961
 962        Outputs:
 963            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the body contour 
 964                    in the dicom structure file. It will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
 965        """
 966
 967        if body_index_range is None or body_mask_shape is None:
 968            assert pth_dir_dicom is not None, "Either path to a dicom directory with dicom structure \
 969                file should be given or body_index_range and body_mask_shape"
 970            # body_index_range, body_mask_shape = get_structure_index_range(pth_dir_dicom)
 971        # the body mask may have a different size than the dose map, we normalize range to the dimension
 972        # of original mask and scale it to the dimension of the dose map to get the body index range on the dose image.
 973        scaled_body_index_range = (body_index_range / np.expand_dims(
 974            body_mask_shape, axis=1) * np.expand_dims(self.num_voxels, axis=1)).astype(int)
 975
 976        self.crop_by_index(scaled_body_index_range, True)
 977
 978    def multiply_dose_by_constant(
 979        self, 
 980        scale_factor: float, 
 981        scale_uncert: Optional[bool] = False):
 982        r"""
 983        Purpose: 
 984            scale the dose and uncertainty maps by a constant factor. 
 985        Inputs:
 986            - scale_factor := a floating point number that the dose and uncertainty maps will be scaled by. 
 987        Outputs:
 988            - Void := will scale the dose and uncertainty maps of self by the scale factor. 
 989        """
 990        self.is_not_empty()
 991        self.grid *= scale_factor
 992        if scale_uncert and self.uncertainty is not None:
 993            self.uncertainty *= scale_factor

1236class DoseComparison:
1237
1238    def __init__(self, dose1: BrachyDose, dose2: BrachyDose, gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float,
1239                 gamma_distance_threshold_mm: float, compute_percent_difference=True, compute_gamma_index=True,
1240                 prescription_dose: float = None, max_gamma = None, path = None,
1241                 gamma_kwargs: dict = {'lower_percent_dose_cutoff': 5, 'interp_fraction': 10,
1242                                       'local_gamma': False, 'global_normalisation': None, 'skip_once_passed': False}):
1243        #provide no dose to just load a file
1244        if(dose1 is None and dose2 is None):
1245            self.load_comparison_object(path)
1246            return
1247        
1248        self.dose1 = dose1
1249        self.dose2 = dose2
1250        # axis is taken from the first dose provided
1251        self.voxel_centers = dose1.get_voxel_centers()
1252        self.dose_2_grid_resampled = self.dose2.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
1253            self.voxel_centers[2], self.voxel_centers[1], self.voxel_centers[0])
1254        self.percent_difference: BrachyDose = None
1255        self.gamma_index: BrachyDose = None
1256        self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold = gamma_dose_percent_threshold
1257        self.gamma_kwargs = gamma_kwargs
1258        #we can index the dose cutoff to the prescription dose
1259        if(isinstance(prescription_dose, float) or isinstance(prescription_dose, int)):
1260            self.gamma_kwargs["global_normalisation"] = prescription_dose
1261        if(isinstance(max_gamma, float) or isinstance(prescription_dose, int)):
1262            self.max_gamma = max_gamma
1263            self.gamma_kwargs["max_gamma"] = max_gamma
1264        else:
1265            self.max_gamma = 2
1266        # axes values are assumed in cm from the 3ddose formalism
1267        # gamma distance thresholds are usually provided in mm
1268        # pymedphys documentation indicates that the threshold unit must match the axis
1269        # despite the name of the function input containing 'mm'
1270        self.gamma_distance_threshold = gamma_distance_threshold_mm / 10.0
1271        if (compute_percent_difference):
1272            self.compute_percent_difference()
1273        if (compute_gamma_index):
1274            self.compute_gamma_index()
1275
1276    def plot_2d_dose_comparison(self, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str, plot_titles: tuple):
1277        import itertools
1278        import matplotlib
1279        from matplotlib.ticker import (MultipleLocator, FormatStrFormatter, AutoMinorLocator)
1280        matplotlib.rcParams.update({'font.size': 16})
1281        dose_1_profile = self.dose1.extract_profile_2d(
1282            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1283        dose_2_profile = self.dose2.extract_profile_2d(
1284            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1285        if (self.percent_difference is not None):
1286            percent_difference_profile = self.percent_difference.extract_profile_2d(
1287                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1288        if (self.gamma_index is not None):
1289            gamma_index_profile = self.gamma_index.extract_profile_2d(
1290                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1291        else:
1292            raise NotImplementedError("""Plotting of a comparison without computing the percent difference or
1293            gamma index is not supported""")
1294        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10), nrows=2, ncols=2, sharex=True, sharey=True)
1295        plt.tight_layout()
1296        c00 = ax[0, 0].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, dose_1_profile, vmin=0,
1297                              vmax=30, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1298        ax[0, 0].set_title(plot_titles[0], fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1299        cbar00 = fig.colorbar(c00, ax=ax[0, 0])
1300        cbar00.set_label(label='Dose [Gy]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1301        # cbar00.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)
1302        ax[0, 0].invert_yaxis()
1303        ax[0, 0].set_ylabel('y (cm)', fontsize=18)
1304        c01 = ax[0, 1].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, dose_2_profile, vmin=0,
1305                              vmax=30, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1306        ax[0, 1].set_title(plot_titles[1], fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1307        cbar01 = fig.colorbar(c01, ax=ax[0, 1])
1308        cbar01.set_label(label='Dose [Gy]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1309        # cbar01.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)
1310        ax[0, 1].invert_yaxis()
1311        c10 = ax[1, 0].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, percent_difference_profile,
1312                              vmin=0, vmax=200, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1313        ax[1, 0].set_title('Percent Difference', fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1314        cbar10 = fig.colorbar(c10, ax=ax[1, 0])
1315        cbar10.set_label(label='[%]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1316        ax[1, 0].invert_yaxis()
1317        ax[1, 0].set_xlabel('x (cm)', fontsize=18)
1318        ax[1, 0].set_ylabel('y (cm)', fontsize=18)
1319
1320        c11 = ax[1, 1].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, gamma_index_profile, vmin=0,
1321                              vmax=self.max_gamma,  cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1322        ax[1, 1].set_title(
1323            f"Gamma ({self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold}% / {int(10.*self.gamma_distance_threshold)} mm)", fontsize=20, pad=5, 
1324            fontweight="bold")
1325        #: Pass Rate = {np.round(self.gamma_pass_ratio*100,1)}%"
1326        cbar11 = fig.colorbar(c11, ax=ax[1, 1])
1327        cbar11.set_label(label='Gamma', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1328        ax[1, 1].invert_yaxis()
1329        ax[1, 1].set_xlabel('x (cm)', fontsize=18)
1330        plt.show()
1331
1332    def compute_percent_difference(self):
1333        self.percent_difference = BrachyDose()
1334        self.percent_difference.grid = np.abs(
1335            self.dose1.grid - self.dose_2_grid_resampled) / self.dose1.grid * 100
1336        self.percent_difference.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1337        self.percent_difference.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1338        self.percent_difference.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1339        self.percent_difference.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1340        self.percent_difference.create_interpolation_function()
1341
1342    def compute_gamma_index(self):
1343        print("Computing gamma index may take time")
1344        logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.DEBUG)
1345        self.gamma_index = BrachyDose()
1346        gamma_index_grid = pymedphys.gamma(tuple(self.voxel_centers), self.dose1.grid, tuple(
1347            self.voxel_centers), self.dose_2_grid_resampled, self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold, self.gamma_distance_threshold,
1348            **self.gamma_kwargs)
1349        #cast the NaNs to 0s
1350        number_excluded = np.sum(np.isnan(gamma_index_grid))
1351        gamma_index_grid[np.isnan(gamma_index_grid)] = -1
1352        self.gamma_index.grid = gamma_index_grid
1353        self.gamma_index.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1354        self.gamma_index.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1355        self.gamma_index.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1356        self.gamma_index.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1357        self.gamma_pass_ratio = (np.sum(self.gamma_index.grid <= 1) - number_excluded) / (self.gamma_index.grid.size - number_excluded)
1358        self.gamma_index.create_interpolation_function()
1359
1360    def save_comparison_object(self, path:str = None):
1361        r"""
1362        Saves the dose comparison object to a file using the pickle module.
1363
1364        Returns:
1365        None
1366        """
1367        if not isinstance(path, str):
1368            root = tk.Tk()
1369            root.withdraw()    
1370            f = fd.asksaveasfile(mode='wb',
1371            defaultextension=".comp", initialdir=os.getcwd(),
1372            title='Save dose comparison object', confirmoverwrite=True)
1373            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
1374            root.destroy()
1375            f.close()
1376        else: 
1377            with open(path, 'wb') as f:
1378                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
1379

1381    def load_comparison_object(self, path:str = None):
1382        r"""
1383        Opens the dose comparison object file and updates the current object's attributes with the loaded object's attributes.
1384
1385        Returns:
1386        None
1387        """
1388        if not isinstance(path, str):
1389            root = tk.Tk()
1390            root.withdraw()
1391            f = fd.askopenfile(mode='rb',
1392            parent=root, initialdir="$HOME", title='Select saved dose comparison file')
1393            self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
1394                #print(calibration_object_file_path)
1395            root.destroy()
1396            f.close()
1397        else:
1398            with open(path, 'rb') as f:
1399                self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)

class BrachyDose: 
 61class BrachyDose:
 62    r"""
 63    Purpse: 
 64        This class holds information regarding a dose distribution as well as the fundamental 
 65    functions that are applied on the dose. All the doses are J/Gy. 
 66
 67    Attributes:
 68        grid:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose at each voxel. [z, y, x]
 69        uncertainty:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose uncertainity at each voxel. [z, y, x] 
 70        num_voxels:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the number of grid points on x, y, z axis. 
 71        voxel_size:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the resolution of each voxel along x, y, z axis in centimeters. 
 72        origin_coordinates:np.ndarray := The spatial coordinate of the "bottom" left corner of the image in centrimeters. [x, y, z] 
 73        voxel_edges:np.ndarray := coorindates of voxel edges along z, y and x axis.  
 74
 75    Functions:
 76        load_file_to_brachydose()
 77        load_from_3ddose()
 78        load_from_nrrd()
 79        load_from_npz()
 80        make_profile()
 81        make_pdd()
 82        get_average_uncert()
 83        get_average_uncert_benchmark()
 84        pad_3ddose()
 85        multiply_dose_by_constant()
 86        write_to_3ddose()
 87        write_to_nrrd()
 88        write_to_npz()
 89        write_to_minidos()
 90        write_to_xz()
 91        write_to_zstd()
 92        calculate_voxel_edges()
 93        is_equal()
 94        crop_by_coordinates()
 95        crop_by_fraction()
 96        crop_by_index()
 97        is_not_empty()
 98        info()
 99
100    Dependencies: 
101        numpy
102        re
103        os
104        glob
105        SimpleITK
106        difflib
107        typing
108        collections
109        pytest
110        lzma
111        pickle
112        pyzstd
113        typer
114        tqdm
115        DicomRTTool
116        pydicom
117        json
118    """
119    
120    def __init__(self, pth_dose_file: Optional[str] = None):
121
122        self.grid: np.ndarray = None
123        self.uncertainty: np.ndarray = None
124        self.num_voxels: np.ndarray = None
125        self.voxel_size: np.ndarray = None
126        self.origin_coordinates: np.ndarray = None
127        self.voxel_edges: np.ndarray = None
128        self.interpolation_function = None
129        if pth_dose_file is not None:
130            self.load_file_to_brachydose(pth_dose_file)
131        if self.grid is not None:
132            self.create_interpolation_function()
133      
134    def load_file_to_brachydose(self, pth_dose_file: str):
135        r""" 
136        Purpose: 
137        given the path to a file holding dose information, it will return 
138        a BrachyDose object with the populated available attributes. It will give a warning
139        for the missing attributes.
140
141        Inputs:
142            - pth_dose_file := path directory where the file containing the dose is. The file 
143                extension could be ".3ddose", ".nrrd", ".dcm", or ".minidos"
144
145        Output:
146        self : BrachyDose
147        """
148        pth_dose_file = os.path.abspath(pth_dose_file)
149
150        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
151
152        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
153            self.load_from_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
154        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
155            self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
156        elif file_extension == ".dcm":
157            assert "RD" in pth_dose_file, "must be a dicom dose file starting with 'RD'"
158            raise NotImplementedError(
159                "loading dose from dicom is not currently supported")
160        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
161            raise NotImplementedError(
162                "loading dose from .minidos file is not currently supported")
163        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
164            raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
165        else:
166            raise ValueError("file extension not recognized")
167        #voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
168        # print(len(self.voxel_edges))
169        if(self.interpolation_function is None and self.grid is not None):
170            self.create_interpolation_function()
171        return self
172
173    def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: str):
174        r"""
175        Purpose:
176        To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically
177        detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function. 
178
179        Inputs:
180            - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options 
181            for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd". 
182
183        Output:
184            - void := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"
185        """
186        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
187
188        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
189            self.write_to_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
190
191        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
192            self.write_to_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
193
194        elif file_extension == ".npz":
195            self.write_to_npz(pth_dose_file)
196
197        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
198            self.write_to_minidos(pth_dose_file)
199
200        elif file_extension == ".xz":
201            self.write_to_xz(pth_dose_file)
202
203        elif file_extension == ".zstd":
204            self.write_to_zstd(pth_dose_file)
205
206        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
207           raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
208
209        else:
210            raise ValueError(f"The input file name {pth_dose_file} is not supported. the supported \
211            file types are '.3ddose', '.nrrd', '.npz', '.minidos', '.xz', and '.zstd'")
212
213    def load_from_3ddose(self, filename: str):
214        r""" 
215        Purpose: 
216            Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
217
218        Input:
219            - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file
220        """
221        assert os.path.splitext(
222            filename)[-1] == ".3ddose", "this file should have '3ddose' extension."
223        path = filename
224        # print("Opening 3ddose at %s" % path)
225        with open(path, "rb") as newfile:
226            bench_voxels = [int(i) for i in newfile.readline().split()]
227            bench_x_pos = np.round(
228                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
229            bench_y_pos = np.round(
230                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
231            bench_z_pos = np.round(
232                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
233
234            bench_x_spacing = bench_x_pos[1] - bench_x_pos[0]
235            bench_y_spacing = bench_y_pos[1] - bench_y_pos[0]
236            bench_slice_thick = bench_z_pos[1] - bench_z_pos[0]
237
238            bench_dict = {}
239
240            huge_dose_array = np.array(
241                newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
242            bench_dose = reshape(
243                huge_dose_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
244            try:
245                huge_uncert_array = np.array(
246                    newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
247                bench_uncert = reshape(
248                    huge_uncert_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
249                self.uncertainty = bench_uncert
250            except:
251                print("Warning: No uncertainty in the 3ddose files")
252
253            self.grid = bench_dose
254            self.num_voxels = np.array(bench_voxels, dtype=np.float32)
255            self.voxel_size = np.round(np.array(
256                [bench_x_spacing, bench_y_spacing, bench_slice_thick], dtype=np.float32), 1)
257            self.origin_coordinates = np.array(
258                [bench_x_pos[0], bench_y_pos[0], bench_z_pos[0]], dtype=np.float32)
259            # overriding axis calculation to ignore the axis contents of 3ddose and use the function below
260            # np.array([bench_z_pos, bench_y_pos, bench_x_pos], dtype=object)
261            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
262
263    def load_from_nrrd(self, pth_nrrd: str):
264        r"""
265        Purpose: 
266            given the path to a nrrd dose file, it will load its content into self:BrachyDose
267
268        Inputs: 
269            - pth_nrrd := Path to a nrrd file writtern by self.to_nrrd()
270
271        Dependencies:
272            - SimpleITK
273            - calculate_voxel_edges()
274        """
275        loaded_image_nrrd = sitk.ReadImage(pth_nrrd, imageIO='NrrdImageIO')
276        [dose_array, uncertainty_array] = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(
277            loaded_image_nrrd)
278        dose_array = np.swapaxes(dose_array, 0, 2)
279        uncertainty_array = np.swapaxes(uncertainty_array, 0, 2)
280
281        self.uncertainty = uncertainty_array.astype(np.float32)
282        self.grid = dose_array.astype(np.float32)
283        self.num_voxels = np.array(
284            np.flip((dose_array.shape), axis=0)).astype(np.float32)
285        self.voxel_size = np.round(np.array(loaded_image_nrrd.GetSpacing()[
286                                 1:]).astype(np.float32), 1)
287        self.origin_coordinates = np.array(loaded_image_nrrd.GetOrigin()[
288                                1:]).astype(np.float32)
289        self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()

348    def create_interpolation_function(self):
349        voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
350        self.interpolation_function = RegularGridInterpolator(
351            (voxel_centers[0], voxel_centers[1], voxel_centers[2]), self.grid, bounds_error=False, fill_value = 0)
352
353    def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z):
354        r"""
355        """
356        self.is_not_empty()
357        if (self.interpolation_function is None):
358            raise ValueError("interpolation function is not defined")
359        shape = []
360        axis = []
361        for coord in [z, y, x]:
362            if isinstance(coord, float):
363                coord_size = 1
364                axis.append([coord])
365            elif isinstance(coord, np.ndarray):
366                coord_size = coord.size
367                axis.append(coord)
368            else:
369                raise TypeError(
370                    "x, y, and z should be either floats or numpy arrays")
371            shape.append(coord_size)
372        coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x = np.meshgrid(
373            [z], [y], [x], indexing='ij')
374        # print(coord_grid.shape())
375        dose_grid = self.interpolation_function(
376            (coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x))
377        dose_grid.reshape(shape)
378        return dose_grid.squeeze()
379
380    def extract_profile_2d(self, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str):
381        if not isinstance(axis_1_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(axis_2_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(plane_coord, float):
382            raise TypeError(
383                "axis_1_coords and axis_2_coords should be numpy arrays and plane_coord should be a float")
384        if plane == 'xy':
385            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord)
386        elif plane == 'xz':
387            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, plane_coord, axis_2_coords)
388        elif plane == 'yz':
389            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords)
390        elif plane == 'yx':
391            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, plane_coord)
392        elif plane == 'zx':
393            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, plane_coord, axis_1_coords)
394        elif plane == 'zy':
395            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords)
396        else:
397            raise ValueError(
398                "plane should be one of the following: 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', 'yx', 'zx', 'zy'")
399
400    def extract_profile_1d(self, axis: str, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, axis_3_coords: List[float]) -> np.ndarray:
401        r"""
402        Extracts a 1D line profile from the dose grid along the specified axis, given the coordinates of the other two axes and a list of coordinates along the axis of extraction.
403
404        Parameters:
405            - axis (str): the axis along which to extract the line profile. Must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.
406            - axis_1_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the first axis, as a 1D numpy array.
407            - axis_2_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the second axis, as a 1D numpy array.
408            - axis_3_coords (List[float]): the coordinates along the axis of extraction, as a list of floats.
409
410        Returns:
411            - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.
412        """
413        if axis not in ['x', 'y', 'z']:
414            raise ValueError("axis must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'")
415
416        if axis == 'x':
417            x = np.array(axis_3_coords)
418            y, z = np.meshgrid(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, indexing='ij')
419        elif axis == 'y':
420            y = np.array(axis_3_coords)
421            x, z = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
422        else:
423            z = np.array(axis_3_coords)
424            x, y = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
425
426        dose_grid = self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(x, y, z)
427        profile = np.mean(dose_grid, axis=(1, 2))
428        return profile
429
430        # pdd_dict["x_axis"] = z_values
431        # pdd_dict["y_axis"] = np.array(dose_values)
432        # return pdd_dict

434    def get_average_uncert(self) -> float:
435        r"""
436        Purpose:
437            Documentation is missing
438        """
439        max_dose = self.grid.max()
440        dose_mask = self.grid < 0.2 * max_dose
441        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.uncert, mask=dose_mask)
442        masked_dose = ma.array(self.grid, mask=dose_mask)
443        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert / masked_dose) * 100
444        return average_uncert
445
446    def get_average_uncert_benchmark(self) -> float:
447        r"""
448        Purpose:
449            Documentation is missing
450        """
451        max_dose = self.grid.max()
452        dose_mask = self.grid < 0.2 * max_dose
453        masked_uncert = ma.array(self.uncert, mask=dose_mask)
454        average_uncert = ma.average(masked_uncert) * 100
455        return average_uncert

457    def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_top_left: list):
458        r''' a function to padd the grid and uncertainty in BrachyDose object and bring it to the desired dimensios.
459        it will update all the aspects of the dose object to match the new dimensiosn.
460        The voxels must have the same size! remember, python does z, y, x. 
461        inputs:
462            self:BrachyDose
463
464            new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:
465                [new_z_dim, new_y_dim, new_x_dim]
466
467            new_top_left := coordinates of the new origin_coordinates
468                [x, y, z]
469        '''
470        assert any(
471            new_dims > self.grid.shape), "since you are padding, the new dimensions should be larger than the input dimensions"
472
473        # calculate distances between the new and old origin_coordinates voxels.
474        # if for an axis, the distance of origin_coordinatess is larger than the voxel size, use the new origin_coordinates
475        # else, use the old top left
476        origin_coordinates_distance = np.abs(new_top_left - self.origin_coordinates)
477        final_origin_coordinates = np.zeros(3)
478        for i, distance in zip(range(3), origin_coordinates_distance):
479            final_origin_coordinates[i] = new_top_left[i] if distance > self.voxel_size[i] else self.origin_coordinates[i]
480
481        # figure out how much padding to do before and after each axis
482        padding = np.zeros([3, 2])
483        for i in range(3):
484            if final_origin_coordinates[i] == self.origin_coordinates[i]:
485                # all padding goes to the end for this dose axis
486                pad_before = 0
487                pad_after = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
488            else:
489                # all padding goes to the begining of the dose axis
490                pad_before = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
491                pad_after = 0
492            padding[2-i] = [pad_before, pad_after]
493
494        # pad the old dose grid to get the new grid!
495        new_dose_grid = np.pad(self.grid, tuple(
496            padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
497        if self.uncertainty is not None:
498            new_uncert = np.pad(self.uncertainty, tuple(
499                padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
500
501        # figure out the end coordinates based on the padding
502        # self.voxel_size is a list of x, y and z spacing, we want it to be
503        # a numpy array of z, y, x spacings.
504        voxel_size = np.array(self.voxel_size)[:, np.newaxis][::-1]
505        end_coords_distances = padding * \
506            np.array([[-1, 1], [-1, 1], [-1, 1]]) * voxel_size
507
508        old_end_coords = np.array(
509            [[self.voxel_edges[0][0], self.voxel_edges[0][-1]],
510             [self.voxel_edges[1][0], self.voxel_edges[1][-1]],
511             [self.voxel_edges[2][0], self.voxel_edges[2][-1]]])
512
513        new_end_coords = old_end_coords + end_coords_distances
514
515        # now padd the new axis with respect to the appropriate begin and end coordinates
516        new_axis = np.array([np.zeros(new_dims[0]), np.zeros(
517            new_dims[1]), np.zeros(new_dims[2])], dtype=object)
518
519        # pad the new axis with linear ramp
520        for i in range(new_axis.shape[0]):
521            new_axis[i] = np.pad(self.voxel_edges[i], tuple(padding[i].astype(
522                int)), mode='linear_ramp', end_values=new_end_coords[i])
523
524        # fillout the new padded dose dictionary
525        padded_dose = BrachyDose()
526
527        padded_dose.grid = new_dose_grid
528        padded_dose.uncert = new_uncert if self.uncertainty is not None else None
529        # voxel size remains unchanged
530        padded_dose.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
531        padded_dose.origin_coordinates = final_origin_coordinates
532        padded_dose.voxel_edges = new_axis
533
534        return padded_dose
535
536    def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str):
537        r''' 
538        Purpose: 
539            This function will write the contents of a BrachyDose onto a text file with .3ddose extension. 
540
541        inputs:
542            - self := a BrachyDose object containing the following keys:
543                grid [z, y, x]
544                uncert [z, y, x] 
545                voxel_size [x, y, z]
546                origin_coordinates [x, y, z]
547                axis [z, y, x]
548
549            - file_name := the directory path where the file will be written
550        '''
551        file_name = os.path.abspath(file_name)
552
553        dimensions = ' '.join(map(str, self.num_voxels.astype(int))) + '\n'
554        x_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[2])) + '\n'
555        y_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[1])) + '\n'
556        z_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[0])) + '\n'
557        dose_flattened = ' '.join(map(str, self.grid.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
558        if self.uncertainty is not None:
559            uncertainty_flattened = ' '.join(
560                map(str, self.uncertainty.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
561        else:
562            uncertainty_flattened = ''
563
564        with open(file_name, 'w') as file:
565            lines = [dimensions, x_axis, y_axis, z_axis,
566                     dose_flattened, uncertainty_flattened]
567            file.writelines(lines)
568
569    def write_to_nrrd(self, file_name: str, metadata: Optional[dict] = None):
570        r"""
571            Purpose: 
572                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file. 
573            inputs:
574                - file_name := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to. 
575
576                - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later):
577                    "cancer site": 
578                    "care center": 
579                    "number of dwell positions": 
580                    "number of segmented structures": 
581                    "patient number": 
582                    "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]"
583            outputs: Void
584                writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd
585                note that 3D dose files are written in z, y, x, but the sitk image is written in x, y, z. 
586        """
587        # create sitk dose image
588        dose_nda = np.swapaxes(self.grid, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
589        uncertainty_nda = np.swapaxes(
590            self.uncertainty, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
591
592        image_nrrd = sitk.JoinSeries(
593            sitk.GetImageFromArray(dose_nda),
594            sitk.GetImageFromArray(uncertainty_nda)
595        )
596        image_nrrd.SetOrigin(np.append([0], self.origin_coordinates))
597        image_nrrd.SetSpacing(np.append([1], self.voxel_size))
598
599        # set the metadata: all sitk Images belonging to a patient will have the same meta data
600        if metadata is not None:
601            for key in metadata:
602                image_nrrd.SetMetaData(key, metadata[key])
603
604        # write out the files
605        file_name_ospth = os.path.abspath(file_name)
606        assert os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(
607            file_name_ospth)), f"the input folder does not exist: {os.path.dirname(file_name_ospth)}"
608
609        run_number = file_name_ospth.split(".")[0]
610
611        sitk.WriteImage(image_nrrd, run_number+".nrrd",
612                        useCompression=True, compressionLevel=9)
613
614    def write_to_npz(self, file_name: str):
615        r"""
616            Purpose: 
617                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a npz file, which is numpy compressed. 
618
619            inputs:
620                - self := BrachyDose object
621                - file_name := path where the dose npz file will be written to. 
622
623            outputs: Void
624                writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name. 
625        """
626
627        assert os.path.splitext(file_name)[-1] == ".npz"
628
629        np.savez_compressed(
630            file=file_name,
631            grid=self.grid,
632            uncertainty=self.uncertainty,
633            num_voxels=self.num_voxels,
634            voxel_size=self.voxel_size,
635            origin_coordinates=self.origin_coordinates,
636            axis=self.voxel_edges,
637        )
638
639    def write_to_minidos(self, file_name, compress_program: Optional[str] = None):
640        r"""
641            Purpose: 
642                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a minidos file, which is just a binary file written line by line. 
643                This code is based on Maude Robitaille's implementation. 
644                This script was developed by Maude Robitaille. 
645            inputs:
646                - self := BrachyDose object
647                - file_name := path where the dose minidos file will be written to. 
648
649            outputs: Void
650                writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name. 
651        """
652        assert os.path.splitext(
653            file_name)[-1] == ".minidos", f"the file name {file_name} should have '.minidos' extension."
654        with open(file_name, 'wb') as newfile:
655
656            # the first line is the number of voxels along each dimension [x, y , z]
657            dims_array = array('i', self.num_voxels)
658            dims_array.tofile(newfile)
659
660            # lines 2,3 and 4 are the voxel sizes x, y, z
661            float_array_x = array('f', [self.voxel_size[0]])
662            float_array_x.tofile(newfile)
663            float_array_y = array('f', [self.voxel_size[1]])
664            float_array_y.tofile(newfile)
665            float_array_z = array('f', [self.voxel_size[2]])
666            float_array_z.tofile(newfile)
667
668            # lines 5, 6, 7 are the origins x, y, and z
669            originx_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[0]])
670            originy_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[1]])
671            originz_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[2]])
672
673            originx_array.tofile(newfile)
674            originy_array.tofile(newfile)
675            originz_array.tofile(newfile)
676
677            # lines 8 is just a zero
678            zero = array('i', [0])
679            zero.tofile(newfile)
680
681            # line 9-infinit is the dose per voxel array
682            for d in self.grid.flatten():
683                array('f', [d]).tofile(newfile)
684
685    def write_to_xz(self, fileName):
686        assert os.path.splitext(fileName)[-1] == '.xz'
687
688        with lzma.open(fileName, 'wb') as file:
689            pickle.dump(self, file)

691    def write_to_zstd(self, file_name):
692        assert os.path.splitext(file_name)[-1] == '.zst'
693
694        with pyzstd.open(file_name, "wb", level_or_option=22) as file:
695            pickle.dump(self, file, protocol=pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
