697    def calculate_voxel_edges(self):
698        r"""
699        Purpose: will calculate the axies coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary.
700        Input: 
701            - dose := output of load_3ddose(). it should have the following keys and values:
702                {"grid":,
703                "origin_coordinates":,
704                "voxel_size":}
705        Output: 
706            - axes:numpy.array() := 
707            [[z_min:voxel_size:z_max],
708            [y_min:voxel_size:y_max],
709            [x_min:voxel_size:x_max]] 
710        """
711        # calculate the end point of axis in 3D space
712        axes_end = np.array(
713            # one voxel size is added because np.arange stops at an index before the end
714            self.origin_coordinates + self.num_voxels * self.voxel_size + self.voxel_size
715        )
716                
717        self.voxel_edges = np.empty(len(axes_end), dtype=object)
718        for i in range(len(axes_end)):
719            self.voxel_edges[i] = np.arange(
720                self.origin_coordinates[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
721                axes_end[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
722                self.voxel_size[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
723                dtype=np.float32)
724            if np.absolute(self.grid.shape[i] - self.voxel_edges[i].shape[0]) > 1:
725                self.voxel_edges[i] = self.voxel_edges[i][:-1] 
726
727        return self.voxel_edges
728
729    def get_voxel_centers(self):
730        voxel_centers = np.empty(len(self.voxel_edges), dtype=object)
731        if self.voxel_edges is not None:
732            for i in range(len(self.voxel_edges)):
733                voxel_centers[i] = self.voxel_edges[i] + self.voxel_size[i]/2.
734                voxel_centers[i] = voxel_centers[i][:-1]
735        else:
736            raise ValueError("Voxel edges are not calculated yet")
737        return voxel_centers
738
739    def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose):
740        r"""
741        Purpose:
742            To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose
743
744        Inputs:
745            - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain equal info as the attributes of self. 
746
747        Outputs:
748            True if attributes of new_brachy_dose are the same as self
749            False otherwise
750        """
751        assert isinstance(
752            new_brachy_dose, BrachyDose), "input must be of type BrachyDose"
753        assert np.array_equal(
754            self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid), "dose grid is not the same"
755        assert np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(
756            new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)), "axis is not the same"
757        assert np.array_equal(
758            self.uncertainty, new_brachy_dose.uncertainty), "uncertainty is not the same"
759        assert np.array_equal(
760            self.num_voxels, new_brachy_dose.num_voxels), "num_voxels is not the same"
761        assert np.array_equal(
762            self.voxel_size, new_brachy_dose.voxel_size), "voxel_size is not the same"
763        assert np.array_equal(
764            self.origin_coordinates, new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), "origin_coordinates is not the same"
765        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)), "voxel_size is not the same"
766        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2), "origin_coordinates is not the same"
767
768        return np.array_equal(self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid) \
769            and np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)) \
770            and np.array_equal(self.uncertainty, new_brachy_dose.uncertainty) \
771            and np.array_equal(self.num_voxels, new_brachy_dose.num_voxels) \
772            and np.array_equal(self.voxel_size, new_brachy_dose.voxel_size) \
773            and np.array_equal(self.origin_coordinates, new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates)
774        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)) \
775        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2)
776        # np.array_equal(np.round(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), 2), np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)) \
777
778    def crop_by_coordinates(self, coord_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
779        r"""
780        Purpose: 
781            given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
782            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
783        Inputs:
784            - self: BrachyDose object
785            - coord_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
786                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
787        Output:
788            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
789                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
790        Dependencies:
791            -self.crop_by_index()
792        """
793        self.is_not_empty()
794
795        # make sure the ending coordinate of the new range is larger than its origin
796        for ax in coord_range:
797            assert ax[1] > ax[0], "axis ending coordinate should be larger than its begining coordinate"
798
799        # assert coordinate range falls into the image
800        axes_name = ["x axis(2)", "y axis(1)", "z axis(0)"]
801        coords_flipped = np.flip(coord_range, 0)
802        for i in range(self.voxel_edges.shape[0]):
803            assert coords_flipped[i][0] > self.voxel_edges[i][
804                0], f"cropping lower limit must be larger than the lowest coordinate on {axes_name[i]}"
805
806        # convert new coordinates to indicies for both beggingn and ending (may not be exact)
807        new_origin_distance = coord_range[:, 0] - self.origin_coordinates
808
809        new_origin_index = np.floor(
810            new_origin_distance / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
811
812        new_ending_index = np.floor(
813            (coord_range[:, 1] - self.origin_coordinates) / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
814
815        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
816
817        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)
818
819    def crop_by_fraction(self, crop_fraction, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
820        r"""
821        Purpose: 
822            given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)*dimension voxels
823                from the edges of the x and y axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
824        Inputs:
825            - self: BrachyDose object
826            - crop_fraction := a floating point between 0 and 1, which is the fraction of the image axis that remains in the crop. 
827                for example, a crop ratio of 0.5 will keep the center of the x and y axis, plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. 
828                The z axis will not be cropped. 
829                    +++++++++       ---------
830                    +++++++++       --+++++--
831                    +++++++++  ===> --+++++--
832                    +++++++++       --+++++--
833                    +++++++++       ---------
834        Output:
835            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
836                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
837        Dependencies:
838            -self.crop_by_index()
839        """
840        assert crop_fraction >= 0 and crop_fraction <= 1, "the fraction should be between 0 and 1"
841        off_set = 0.5 * (1-crop_fraction)*self.num_voxels
842        new_origin_index = np.array([off_set[0], off_set[1], 0]).astype(int)
843        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
844                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
845
846        new_ending_index = np.array(
847            [self.num_voxels[0]-off_set[0], self.num_voxels[1]-off_set[1], self.num_voxels[2]]).astype(int)
848        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
849                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
850
851        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
852
853        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)
854
855    def crop_by_index(self, index_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
856        r"""
857        Purpose: 
858            given a range of indicies (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
859            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
860        Inputs:
861            - self: BrachyDose object
862            - index_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
863                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
864        Output:
865            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the index range. 
866                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
867        Dependencies:
868            - None
869        """
870        new_origin_index = index_range[:, 0].astype(int)
871        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
872                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
873
874        new_ending_index = index_range[:, 1].astype(int)
875        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
876                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
877
878        # update the attributes
879        if inplace:
880            self.grid = self.grid[
881                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
882                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
883                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
884            ]
885            self.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
886                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
887                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
888                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
889            ]
890            self.origin_coordinates = np.array([
891                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
892                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
893                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
894            ])
895            self.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
896            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
897        else:
898            new_dose_obj = BrachyDose()
899            new_dose_obj.grid = self.grid[
900                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
901                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
902                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
903            ]
904            new_dose_obj.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
905                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
906                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
907                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
908            ]
909            new_dose_obj.origin_coordinates = np.array([
910                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
911                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
912                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
913            ])
914            new_dose_obj.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
915            new_dose_obj.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
916            new_dose_obj.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
917            return new_dose_obj
918
919    def is_not_empty(self):
920        assert self.grid is not None, "error grid is None"
921        # commenting out the following line, since uncertainty is not always available
922        # e.g. for gamma and percent difference
923        # assert self.uncertainty is not None, "error uncertainty is None"
924        assert self.num_voxels is not None, "error num_voxels is None"
925        assert self.voxel_size is not None, "error voxel_size is None"
926        assert self.origin_coordinates is not None, "error origin_coordinates is None"
927        assert self.voxel_edges is not None, "error axis is None"
928        return True

946    def crop_by_body_contour(self, body_index_range: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
947                             body_mask_shape: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
948                             pth_dir_dicom: Optional[str] = None, ):
949        r"""
950        Purpose: 
951            based on the given dicom structure file, crop the BrachyDose object such 
952                that it only has the body contour. 
953        Inputs: 
954            - pth_dir_dicom := pth_dir_dicom := path to the directory with the dicom files of a patient. 
955                it should contain both images and RTSTRUCT file. this input is optional
956
957            - body_index_range:np.array :=  a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
958                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]],
959
960            - original_mask_dimensions:np.array := 1 x 3 array holding the dimension of the original mask
961
962
963        Outputs:
964            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the body contour 
965                    in the dicom structure file. It will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
966        """
967
968        if body_index_range is None or body_mask_shape is None:
969            assert pth_dir_dicom is not None, "Either path to a dicom directory with dicom structure \
970                file should be given or body_index_range and body_mask_shape"
971            # body_index_range, body_mask_shape = get_structure_index_range(pth_dir_dicom)
972        # the body mask may have a different size than the dose map, we normalize range to the dimension
973        # of original mask and scale it to the dimension of the dose map to get the body index range on the dose image.
974        scaled_body_index_range = (body_index_range / np.expand_dims(
975            body_mask_shape, axis=1) * np.expand_dims(self.num_voxels, axis=1)).astype(int)
976
977        self.crop_by_index(scaled_body_index_range, True)
978
979    def multiply_dose_by_constant(
980        self, 
981        scale_factor: float, 
982        scale_uncert: Optional[bool] = False):
983        r"""
984        Purpose: 
985            scale the dose and uncertainty maps by a constant factor. 
986        Inputs:
987            - scale_factor := a floating point number that the dose and uncertainty maps will be scaled by. 
988        Outputs:
989            - Void := will scale the dose and uncertainty maps of self by the scale factor. 
990        """
991        self.is_not_empty()
992        self.grid *= scale_factor
993        if scale_uncert and self.uncertainty is not None:
994            self.uncertainty *= scale_factor

Purpse: This class holds information regarding a dose distribution as well as the fundamental functions that are applied on the dose. All the doses are J/Gy.

Attributes: grid:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose at each voxel. [z, y, x] uncertainty:np.ndarray := 3D numpy array holding dose uncertainity at each voxel. [z, y, x] num_voxels:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the number of grid points on x, y, z axis. voxel_size:np.ndarray := 1D numpy array holding the resolution of each voxel along x, y, z axis in centimeters. origin_coordinates:np.ndarray := The spatial coordinate of the "bottom" left corner of the image in centrimeters. [x, y, z] voxel_edges:np.ndarray := coorindates of voxel edges along z, y and x axis.

Functions: load_file_to_brachydose() load_from_3ddose() load_from_nrrd() load_from_npz() make_profile() make_pdd() get_average_uncert() get_average_uncert_benchmark() pad_3ddose() multiply_dose_by_constant() write_to_3ddose() write_to_nrrd() write_to_npz() write_to_minidos() write_to_xz() write_to_zstd() calculate_voxel_edges() is_equal() crop_by_coordinates() crop_by_fraction() crop_by_index() is_not_empty() info()

def load_file_to_brachydose(self, pth_dose_file: str): 
134    def load_file_to_brachydose(self, pth_dose_file: str):
135        r""" 
136        Purpose: 
137        given the path to a file holding dose information, it will return 
138        a BrachyDose object with the populated available attributes. It will give a warning
139        for the missing attributes.
140
141        Inputs:
142            - pth_dose_file := path directory where the file containing the dose is. The file 
143                extension could be ".3ddose", ".nrrd", ".dcm", or ".minidos"
144
145        Output:
146        self : BrachyDose
147        """
148        pth_dose_file = os.path.abspath(pth_dose_file)
149
150        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
151
152        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
153            self.load_from_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
154        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
155            self.load_from_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
156        elif file_extension == ".dcm":
157            assert "RD" in pth_dose_file, "must be a dicom dose file starting with 'RD'"
158            raise NotImplementedError(
159                "loading dose from dicom is not currently supported")
160        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
161            raise NotImplementedError(
162                "loading dose from .minidos file is not currently supported")
163        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
164            raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
165        else:
166            raise ValueError("file extension not recognized")
167        #voxel_centers = self.get_voxel_centers()
168        # print(len(self.voxel_edges))
169        if(self.interpolation_function is None and self.grid is not None):
170            self.create_interpolation_function()
171        return self

def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: str): 
173    def write_brachydose_to_file(self, pth_dose_file: str):
174        r"""
175        Purpose:
176        To write a brachy dose object to the given file path. this function will automatically
177        detect the type of the output file and will call the right brachyDose writer function. 
178
179        Inputs:
180            - pth_dose_file := path where the BrachyDose contents will be written to. The options 
181            for output type are "3ddose", "nrrd", "npz", "minidos", "xz", and "zstd". 
182
183        Output:
184            - void := contents of self is written to "pth_dose_file"
185        """
186        file_extension = os.path.splitext(pth_dose_file)[-1]
187
188        if file_extension == ".3ddose":
189            self.write_to_3ddose(pth_dose_file)
190
191        elif file_extension == ".nrrd":
192            self.write_to_nrrd(pth_dose_file)
193
194        elif file_extension == ".npz":
195            self.write_to_npz(pth_dose_file)
196
197        elif file_extension == ".minidos":
198            self.write_to_minidos(pth_dose_file)
199
200        elif file_extension == ".xz":
201            self.write_to_xz(pth_dose_file)
202
203        elif file_extension == ".zstd":
204            self.write_to_zstd(pth_dose_file)
205
206        elif file_extension == ".bindose":
207           raise NotImplementedError("Writing to .bindose not implemented")
208
209        else:
210            raise ValueError(f"The input file name {pth_dose_file} is not supported. the supported \
211            file types are '.3ddose', '.nrrd', '.npz', '.minidos', '.xz', and '.zstd'")

def load_from_3ddose(self, filename: str): 
213    def load_from_3ddose(self, filename: str):
214        r""" 
215        Purpose: 
216            Given the path to a 3ddose file, load its content into self:BrachyDose.
217
218        Input:
219            - filename := path to a ".3ddose" file
220        """
221        assert os.path.splitext(
222            filename)[-1] == ".3ddose", "this file should have '3ddose' extension."
223        path = filename
224        # print("Opening 3ddose at %s" % path)
225        with open(path, "rb") as newfile:
226            bench_voxels = [int(i) for i in newfile.readline().split()]
227            bench_x_pos = np.round(
228                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
229            bench_y_pos = np.round(
230                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
231            bench_z_pos = np.round(
232                np.array(newfile.readline().split(), dtype=np.float32), decimals=6)
233
234            bench_x_spacing = bench_x_pos[1] - bench_x_pos[0]
235            bench_y_spacing = bench_y_pos[1] - bench_y_pos[0]
236            bench_slice_thick = bench_z_pos[1] - bench_z_pos[0]
237
238            bench_dict = {}
239
240            huge_dose_array = np.array(
241                newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
242            bench_dose = reshape(
243                huge_dose_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
244            try:
245                huge_uncert_array = np.array(
246                    newfile.readline().strip().split(), dtype=np.float32)
247                bench_uncert = reshape(
248                    huge_uncert_array, (bench_voxels[2], bench_voxels[1], bench_voxels[0]))
249                self.uncertainty = bench_uncert
250            except:
251                print("Warning: No uncertainty in the 3ddose files")
252
253            self.grid = bench_dose
254            self.num_voxels = np.array(bench_voxels, dtype=np.float32)
255            self.voxel_size = np.round(np.array(
256                [bench_x_spacing, bench_y_spacing, bench_slice_thick], dtype=np.float32), 1)
257            self.origin_coordinates = np.array(
258                [bench_x_pos[0], bench_y_pos[0], bench_z_pos[0]], dtype=np.float32)
259            # overriding axis calculation to ignore the axis contents of 3ddose and use the function below
260            # np.array([bench_z_pos, bench_y_pos, bench_x_pos], dtype=object)
261            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()

def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z): 
353    def extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(self, x, y, z):
354        r"""
355        """
356        self.is_not_empty()
357        if (self.interpolation_function is None):
358            raise ValueError("interpolation function is not defined")
359        shape = []
360        axis = []
361        for coord in [z, y, x]:
362            if isinstance(coord, float):
363                coord_size = 1
364                axis.append([coord])
365            elif isinstance(coord, np.ndarray):
366                coord_size = coord.size
367                axis.append(coord)
368            else:
369                raise TypeError(
370                    "x, y, and z should be either floats or numpy arrays")
371            shape.append(coord_size)
372        coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x = np.meshgrid(
373            [z], [y], [x], indexing='ij')
374        # print(coord_grid.shape())
375        dose_grid = self.interpolation_function(
376            (coord_grid_z, coord_grid_y, coord_grid_x))
377        dose_grid.reshape(shape)
378        return dose_grid.squeeze()
def extract_profile_2d( self, axis_1_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_2_coords: numpy.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str): 
380    def extract_profile_2d(self, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str):
381        if not isinstance(axis_1_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(axis_2_coords, np.ndarray) or not isinstance(plane_coord, float):
382            raise TypeError(
383                "axis_1_coords and axis_2_coords should be numpy arrays and plane_coord should be a float")
384        if plane == 'xy':
385            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord)
386        elif plane == 'xz':
387            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_1_coords, plane_coord, axis_2_coords)
388        elif plane == 'yz':
389            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords)
390        elif plane == 'yx':
391            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, plane_coord)
392        elif plane == 'zx':
393            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(axis_2_coords, plane_coord, axis_1_coords)
394        elif plane == 'zy':
395            return self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(plane_coord, axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords)
396        else:
397            raise ValueError(
398                "plane should be one of the following: 'xy', 'xz', 'yz', 'yx', 'zx', 'zy'")
def extract_profile_1d( self, axis: str, axis_1_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_2_coords: numpy.ndarray, axis_3_coords: List[float]) -> numpy.ndarray: 
400    def extract_profile_1d(self, axis: str, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, axis_3_coords: List[float]) -> np.ndarray:
401        r"""
402        Extracts a 1D line profile from the dose grid along the specified axis, given the coordinates of the other two axes and a list of coordinates along the axis of extraction.
403
404        Parameters:
405            - axis (str): the axis along which to extract the line profile. Must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.
406            - axis_1_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the first axis, as a 1D numpy array.
407            - axis_2_coords (np.ndarray): the coordinates of the second axis, as a 1D numpy array.
408            - axis_3_coords (List[float]): the coordinates along the axis of extraction, as a list of floats.
409
410        Returns:
411            - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.
412        """
413        if axis not in ['x', 'y', 'z']:
414            raise ValueError("axis must be one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'")
415
416        if axis == 'x':
417            x = np.array(axis_3_coords)
418            y, z = np.meshgrid(axis_2_coords, axis_1_coords, indexing='ij')
419        elif axis == 'y':
420            y = np.array(axis_3_coords)
421            x, z = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
422        else:
423            z = np.array(axis_3_coords)
424            x, y = np.meshgrid(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, indexing='ij')
425
426        dose_grid = self.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(x, y, z)
427        profile = np.mean(dose_grid, axis=(1, 2))
428        return profile

432        # return pdd_dict

Returns: - profile (np.ndarray): the line profile extracted from the dose grid, as a 1D numpy array.

434    def get_average_uncert(self) -> float:

439        max_dose = self.grid.max()

def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_top_left: list): 
457    def pad_3ddose(self, new_dims: list, new_top_left: list):
458        r''' a function to padd the grid and uncertainty in BrachyDose object and bring it to the desired dimensios.
459        it will update all the aspects of the dose object to match the new dimensiosn.
460        The voxels must have the same size! remember, python does z, y, x. 
461        inputs:
462            self:BrachyDose
463
464            new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:
465                [new_z_dim, new_y_dim, new_x_dim]
466
467            new_top_left := coordinates of the new origin_coordinates
468                [x, y, z]
469        '''
470        assert any(
471            new_dims > self.grid.shape), "since you are padding, the new dimensions should be larger than the input dimensions"
472
473        # calculate distances between the new and old origin_coordinates voxels.
474        # if for an axis, the distance of origin_coordinatess is larger than the voxel size, use the new origin_coordinates
475        # else, use the old top left
476        origin_coordinates_distance = np.abs(new_top_left - self.origin_coordinates)
477        final_origin_coordinates = np.zeros(3)
478        for i, distance in zip(range(3), origin_coordinates_distance):
479            final_origin_coordinates[i] = new_top_left[i] if distance > self.voxel_size[i] else self.origin_coordinates[i]
480
481        # figure out how much padding to do before and after each axis
482        padding = np.zeros([3, 2])
483        for i in range(3):
484            if final_origin_coordinates[i] == self.origin_coordinates[i]:
485                # all padding goes to the end for this dose axis
486                pad_before = 0
487                pad_after = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
488            else:
489                # all padding goes to the begining of the dose axis
490                pad_before = new_dims[2-i] - self.grid.shape[2-i]
491                pad_after = 0
492            padding[2-i] = [pad_before, pad_after]
493
494        # pad the old dose grid to get the new grid!
495        new_dose_grid = np.pad(self.grid, tuple(
496            padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
497        if self.uncertainty is not None:
498            new_uncert = np.pad(self.uncertainty, tuple(
499                padding.astype(int)), mode='edge')
500
501        # figure out the end coordinates based on the padding
502        # self.voxel_size is a list of x, y and z spacing, we want it to be
503        # a numpy array of z, y, x spacings.
504        voxel_size = np.array(self.voxel_size)[:, np.newaxis][::-1]
505        end_coords_distances = padding * \
506            np.array([[-1, 1], [-1, 1], [-1, 1]]) * voxel_size
507
508        old_end_coords = np.array(
509            [[self.voxel_edges[0][0], self.voxel_edges[0][-1]],
510             [self.voxel_edges[1][0], self.voxel_edges[1][-1]],
511             [self.voxel_edges[2][0], self.voxel_edges[2][-1]]])
512
513        new_end_coords = old_end_coords + end_coords_distances
514
515        # now padd the new axis with respect to the appropriate begin and end coordinates
516        new_axis = np.array([np.zeros(new_dims[0]), np.zeros(
517            new_dims[1]), np.zeros(new_dims[2])], dtype=object)
518
519        # pad the new axis with linear ramp
520        for i in range(new_axis.shape[0]):
521            new_axis[i] = np.pad(self.voxel_edges[i], tuple(padding[i].astype(
522                int)), mode='linear_ramp', end_values=new_end_coords[i])
523
524        # fillout the new padded dose dictionary
525        padded_dose = BrachyDose()
526
527        padded_dose.grid = new_dose_grid
528        padded_dose.uncert = new_uncert if self.uncertainty is not None else None
529        # voxel size remains unchanged
530        padded_dose.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
531        padded_dose.origin_coordinates = final_origin_coordinates
532        padded_dose.voxel_edges = new_axis
533
534        return padded_dose

new_dims := a 1 by 3 list containing the new x, y and z dimensions:

def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str): 
536    def write_to_3ddose(self, file_name: str):
537        r''' 
538        Purpose: 
539            This function will write the contents of a BrachyDose onto a text file with .3ddose extension. 
540
541        inputs:
542            - self := a BrachyDose object containing the following keys:
543                grid [z, y, x]
544                uncert [z, y, x] 
545                voxel_size [x, y, z]
546                origin_coordinates [x, y, z]
547                axis [z, y, x]
548
549            - file_name := the directory path where the file will be written
550        '''
551        file_name = os.path.abspath(file_name)
552
553        dimensions = ' '.join(map(str, self.num_voxels.astype(int))) + '\n'
554        x_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[2])) + '\n'
555        y_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[1])) + '\n'
556        z_axis = ' '.join(map(str, self.voxel_edges[0])) + '\n'
557        dose_flattened = ' '.join(map(str, self.grid.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
558        if self.uncertainty is not None:
559            uncertainty_flattened = ' '.join(
560                map(str, self.uncertainty.flatten('C'))) + '\n'
561        else:
562            uncertainty_flattened = ''
563
564        with open(file_name, 'w') as file:
565            lines = [dimensions, x_axis, y_axis, z_axis,
566                     dose_flattened, uncertainty_flattened]
567            file.writelines(lines)

def write_to_nrrd(self, file_name: str, metadata: Optional[dict] = None): 
569    def write_to_nrrd(self, file_name: str, metadata: Optional[dict] = None):
570        r"""
571            Purpose: 
572                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a nrrd file. 
573            inputs:
574                - file_name := path where the dose nrrd file will be written to. 
575
576                - metadata := a dictionary containing the following meta data key values (should be changed later):
577                    "cancer site": 
578                    "care center": 
579                    "number of dwell positions": 
580                    "number of segmented structures": 
581                    "patient number": 
582                    "Image content": "[3D dose, 3D uncertainty]"
583            outputs: Void
584                writes [3D dose, 3D uncertainty], voxel size, origin (origin_coordinates), and metadata to the file_name_dose.nrrd
585                note that 3D dose files are written in z, y, x, but the sitk image is written in x, y, z. 
586        """
587        # create sitk dose image
588        dose_nda = np.swapaxes(self.grid, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
589        uncertainty_nda = np.swapaxes(
590            self.uncertainty, 0, 2).astype(np.float32)
591
592        image_nrrd = sitk.JoinSeries(
593            sitk.GetImageFromArray(dose_nda),
594            sitk.GetImageFromArray(uncertainty_nda)
595        )
596        image_nrrd.SetOrigin(np.append([0], self.origin_coordinates))
597        image_nrrd.SetSpacing(np.append([1], self.voxel_size))
598
599        # set the metadata: all sitk Images belonging to a patient will have the same meta data
600        if metadata is not None:
601            for key in metadata:
602                image_nrrd.SetMetaData(key, metadata[key])
603
604        # write out the files
605        file_name_ospth = os.path.abspath(file_name)
606        assert os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(
607            file_name_ospth)), f"the input folder does not exist: {os.path.dirname(file_name_ospth)}"
608
609        run_number = file_name_ospth.split(".")[0]
610
611        sitk.WriteImage(image_nrrd, run_number+".nrrd",
612                        useCompression=True, compressionLevel=9)

def write_to_minidos(self, file_name, compress_program: Optional[str] = None): 
639    def write_to_minidos(self, file_name, compress_program: Optional[str] = None):
640        r"""
641            Purpose: 
642                To save the contents of BrachyDose into a minidos file, which is just a binary file written line by line. 
643                This code is based on Maude Robitaille's implementation. 
644                This script was developed by Maude Robitaille. 
645            inputs:
646                - self := BrachyDose object
647                - file_name := path where the dose minidos file will be written to. 
648
649            outputs: Void
650                writes the contents of self:BrachyDose to the file_name. 
651        """
652        assert os.path.splitext(
653            file_name)[-1] == ".minidos", f"the file name {file_name} should have '.minidos' extension."
654        with open(file_name, 'wb') as newfile:
655
656            # the first line is the number of voxels along each dimension [x, y , z]
657            dims_array = array('i', self.num_voxels)
658            dims_array.tofile(newfile)
659
660            # lines 2,3 and 4 are the voxel sizes x, y, z
661            float_array_x = array('f', [self.voxel_size[0]])
662            float_array_x.tofile(newfile)
663            float_array_y = array('f', [self.voxel_size[1]])
664            float_array_y.tofile(newfile)
665            float_array_z = array('f', [self.voxel_size[2]])
666            float_array_z.tofile(newfile)
667
668            # lines 5, 6, 7 are the origins x, y, and z
669            originx_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[0]])
670            originy_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[1]])
671            originz_array = array('f', [self.origin_coordinates[2]])
672
673            originx_array.tofile(newfile)
674            originy_array.tofile(newfile)
675            originz_array.tofile(newfile)
676
677            # lines 8 is just a zero
678            zero = array('i', [0])
679            zero.tofile(newfile)
680
681            # line 9-infinit is the dose per voxel array
682            for d in self.grid.flatten():
683                array('f', [d]).tofile(newfile)

def calculate_voxel_edges(self): 
697    def calculate_voxel_edges(self):
698        r"""
699        Purpose: will calculate the axies coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary.
700        Input: 
701            - dose := output of load_3ddose(). it should have the following keys and values:
702                {"grid":,
703                "origin_coordinates":,
704                "voxel_size":}
705        Output: 
706            - axes:numpy.array() := 
707            [[z_min:voxel_size:z_max],
708            [y_min:voxel_size:y_max],
709            [x_min:voxel_size:x_max]] 
710        """
711        # calculate the end point of axis in 3D space
712        axes_end = np.array(
713            # one voxel size is added because np.arange stops at an index before the end
714            self.origin_coordinates + self.num_voxels * self.voxel_size + self.voxel_size
715        )
716                
717        self.voxel_edges = np.empty(len(axes_end), dtype=object)
718        for i in range(len(axes_end)):
719            self.voxel_edges[i] = np.arange(
720                self.origin_coordinates[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
721                axes_end[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
722                self.voxel_size[len(axes_end)-1-i], 
723                dtype=np.float32)
724            if np.absolute(self.grid.shape[i] - self.voxel_edges[i].shape[0]) > 1:
725                self.voxel_edges[i] = self.voxel_edges[i][:-1] 
726
727        return self.voxel_edges

Purpose: will calculate the axies coordinates for a 3ddose dictionary. Input: - dose := output of load_3ddose(). it should have the following keys and values: {"grid":, "origin_coordinates":, "voxel_size":} Output: - axes:numpy.array() := [[z_min:voxel_size:z_max], [y_min:voxel_size:y_max], [x_min:voxel_size:x_max]]

def get_voxel_centers(self): 
729    def get_voxel_centers(self):
730        voxel_centers = np.empty(len(self.voxel_edges), dtype=object)
731        if self.voxel_edges is not None:
732            for i in range(len(self.voxel_edges)):
733                voxel_centers[i] = self.voxel_edges[i] + self.voxel_size[i]/2.
734                voxel_centers[i] = voxel_centers[i][:-1]
735        else:
736            raise ValueError("Voxel edges are not calculated yet")
737        return voxel_centers
def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose): 
739    def is_equal(self, new_brachy_dose):
740        r"""
741        Purpose:
742            To compare if self:BrachyDose has the same attributes as an input BrachyDose
743
744        Inputs:
745            - new_brachy_dose: another BrachyDose object whose attributes may or may not contain equal info as the attributes of self. 
746
747        Outputs:

749            False otherwise
750        """

752            new_brachy_dose, BrachyDose), "input must be of type BrachyDose"

754            self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid), "dose grid is not the same"
755        assert np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(
756            new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)), "axis is not the same"

765        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)), "voxel_size is not the same"
766        # assert np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2), "origin_coordinates is not the same"
767
768        return np.array_equal(self.grid, new_brachy_dose.grid) \
769            and np.array_equal(np.concatenate(self.voxel_edges), np.concatenate(new_brachy_dose.voxel_edges)) \
770            and np.array_equal(self.uncertainty, new_brachy_dose.uncertainty) \
771            and np.array_equal(self.num_voxels, new_brachy_dose.num_voxels) \
772            and np.array_equal(self.voxel_size, new_brachy_dose.voxel_size) \
773            and np.array_equal(self.origin_coordinates, new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates)
774        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.voxel_size, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.voxel_size, 2)) \
775        # and np.array_equal(np.round(self.origin_coordinates, 2), np.round(new_brachy_dose.origin_coordinates), 2)

def crop_by_coordinates( self, coord_range: <built-in function array>, inplace: Optional[bool] = True): 
778    def crop_by_coordinates(self, coord_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
779        r"""
780        Purpose: 
781            given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
782            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
783        Inputs:
784            - self: BrachyDose object
785            - coord_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
786                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
787        Output:
788            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
789                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
790        Dependencies:
791            -self.crop_by_index()
792        """
793        self.is_not_empty()
794
795        # make sure the ending coordinate of the new range is larger than its origin
796        for ax in coord_range:
797            assert ax[1] > ax[0], "axis ending coordinate should be larger than its begining coordinate"
798
799        # assert coordinate range falls into the image
800        axes_name = ["x axis(2)", "y axis(1)", "z axis(0)"]
801        coords_flipped = np.flip(coord_range, 0)
802        for i in range(self.voxel_edges.shape[0]):
803            assert coords_flipped[i][0] > self.voxel_edges[i][
804                0], f"cropping lower limit must be larger than the lowest coordinate on {axes_name[i]}"
805
806        # convert new coordinates to indicies for both beggingn and ending (may not be exact)
807        new_origin_distance = coord_range[:, 0] - self.origin_coordinates
808
809        new_origin_index = np.floor(
810            new_origin_distance / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
811
812        new_ending_index = np.floor(
813            (coord_range[:, 1] - self.origin_coordinates) / self.voxel_size).astype(int)
814
815        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
816
817        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)

Purpose: given a range of coordinate (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - coord_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] Output: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change Dependencies: -self.crop_by_index()

def crop_by_fraction(self, crop_fraction, inplace: Optional[bool] = True): 
819    def crop_by_fraction(self, crop_fraction, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
820        r"""
821        Purpose: 
822            given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5*(1 - crop_fraction)*dimension voxels
823                from the edges of the x and y axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
824        Inputs:
825            - self: BrachyDose object
826            - crop_fraction := a floating point between 0 and 1, which is the fraction of the image axis that remains in the crop. 
827                for example, a crop ratio of 0.5 will keep the center of the x and y axis, plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. 
828                The z axis will not be cropped. 
829                    +++++++++       ---------
830                    +++++++++       --+++++--
831                    +++++++++  ===> --+++++--
832                    +++++++++       --+++++--
833                    +++++++++       ---------
834        Output:
835            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. 
836                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
837        Dependencies:
838            -self.crop_by_index()
839        """
840        assert crop_fraction >= 0 and crop_fraction <= 1, "the fraction should be between 0 and 1"
841        off_set = 0.5 * (1-crop_fraction)*self.num_voxels
842        new_origin_index = np.array([off_set[0], off_set[1], 0]).astype(int)
843        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
844                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
845
846        new_ending_index = np.array(
847            [self.num_voxels[0]-off_set[0], self.num_voxels[1]-off_set[1], self.num_voxels[2]]).astype(int)
848        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
849                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
850
851        new_index_range = np.column_stack([new_origin_index, new_ending_index])
852
853        return self.crop_by_index(new_index_range, inplace)

Purpose: given the crop_fraction, this function will crop out 0.5(1 - crop_fraction)dimension voxels from the edges of the x and y axis of dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - crop_fraction := a floating point between 0 and 1, which is the fraction of the image axis that remains in the crop. for example, a crop ratio of 0.5 will keep the center of the x and y axis, plus minus 0.25*dimension of the image. The z axis will not be cropped. +++++++++ --------- +++++++++ --+++++-- +++++++++ ===> --+++++-- +++++++++ --+++++-- +++++++++ --------- Output: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the coordinate range. it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change Dependencies: -self.crop_by_index()

def crop_by_index( self, index_range: <built-in function array>, inplace: Optional[bool] = True): 
855    def crop_by_index(self, index_range: np.array, inplace: Optional[bool] = True):
856        r"""
857        Purpose: 
858            given a range of indicies (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop
859            dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. 
860        Inputs:
861            - self: BrachyDose object
862            - index_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
863                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] 
864        Output:
865            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the index range. 
866                it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
867        Dependencies:
868            - None
869        """
870        new_origin_index = index_range[:, 0].astype(int)
871        assert np.all(new_origin_index >=
872                      0), "new origin index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
873
874        new_ending_index = index_range[:, 1].astype(int)
875        assert np.all(new_ending_index >=
876                      0), "new ending index cannot be negative, please report this bug"
877
878        # update the attributes
879        if inplace:
880            self.grid = self.grid[
881                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
882                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
883                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
884            ]
885            self.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
886                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],  # z
887                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],  # y
888                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]  # x
889            ]
890            self.origin_coordinates = np.array([
891                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
892                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
893                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
894            ])
895            self.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
896            self.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
897        else:
898            new_dose_obj = BrachyDose()
899            new_dose_obj.grid = self.grid[
900                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
901                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
902                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
903            ]
904            new_dose_obj.uncertainty = self.uncertainty[
905                new_origin_index[2]:new_ending_index[2],
906                new_origin_index[1]:new_ending_index[1],
907                new_origin_index[0]:new_ending_index[0]
908            ]
909            new_dose_obj.origin_coordinates = np.array([
910                self.voxel_edges[2][new_origin_index[0]],  # x
911                self.voxel_edges[1][new_origin_index[1]],  # y
912                self.voxel_edges[0][new_origin_index[2]]  # z
913            ])
914            new_dose_obj.num_voxels = np.flip(self.grid.shape, 0)
915            new_dose_obj.voxel_size = self.voxel_size
916            new_dose_obj.voxel_edges = self.calculate_voxel_edges()
917            return new_dose_obj

Purpose: given a range of indicies (mix and max on each axis), this function will crop dose and uncertainty maps and will adjust the rest of the attributes accordingly. Inputs: - self: BrachyDose object - index_range := a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]] Output: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the index range. it will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change Dependencies: - None

def crop_by_body_contour( self, body_index_range: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None, body_mask_shape: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None, pth_dir_dicom: Optional[str] = None): 
946    def crop_by_body_contour(self, body_index_range: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
947                             body_mask_shape: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
948                             pth_dir_dicom: Optional[str] = None, ):
949        r"""
950        Purpose: 
951            based on the given dicom structure file, crop the BrachyDose object such 
952                that it only has the body contour. 
953        Inputs: 
954            - pth_dir_dicom := pth_dir_dicom := path to the directory with the dicom files of a patient. 
955                it should contain both images and RTSTRUCT file. this input is optional
956
957            - body_index_range:np.array :=  a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
958                [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]],
959
960            - original_mask_dimensions:np.array := 1 x 3 array holding the dimension of the original mask
961
962
963        Outputs:
964            - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the body contour 
965                    in the dicom structure file. It will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change
966        """
967
968        if body_index_range is None or body_mask_shape is None:
969            assert pth_dir_dicom is not None, "Either path to a dicom directory with dicom structure \
970                file should be given or body_index_range and body_mask_shape"
971            # body_index_range, body_mask_shape = get_structure_index_range(pth_dir_dicom)
972        # the body mask may have a different size than the dose map, we normalize range to the dimension
973        # of original mask and scale it to the dimension of the dose map to get the body index range on the dose image.
974        scaled_body_index_range = (body_index_range / np.expand_dims(
975            body_mask_shape, axis=1) * np.expand_dims(self.num_voxels, axis=1)).astype(int)
976
977        self.crop_by_index(scaled_body_index_range, True)

Purpose: based on the given dicom structure file, crop the BrachyDose object such that it only has the body contour. Inputs: - pth_dir_dicom := pth_dir_dicom := path to the directory with the dicom files of a patient. it should contain both images and RTSTRUCT file. this input is optional

- body_index_range:np.array :=  a 3 x 2 array holding the min and max on x, y and axis
    [[x_min, x_max], [y_min, y_max], [z_min, z_max]],

- original_mask_dimensions:np.array := 1 x 3 array holding the dimension of the original mask

Outputs: - Void := will crop out the dose and uncertainty maps of self to have the range of the body contour in the dicom structure file. It will also update the num_voxels, origin_coordinates and axis. only voxel_size will not change

def multiply_dose_by_constant(self, scale_factor: float, scale_uncert: Optional[bool] = False):

980        self,

class DoseComparison: 
1237class DoseComparison:
1238
1239    def __init__(self, dose1: BrachyDose, dose2: BrachyDose, gamma_dose_percent_threshold: float,
1240                 gamma_distance_threshold_mm: float, compute_percent_difference=True, compute_gamma_index=True,
1241                 prescription_dose: float = None, max_gamma = None, path = None,
1242                 gamma_kwargs: dict = {'lower_percent_dose_cutoff': 5, 'interp_fraction': 10,
1243                                       'local_gamma': False, 'global_normalisation': None, 'skip_once_passed': False}):
1244        #provide no dose to just load a file
1245        if(dose1 is None and dose2 is None):
1246            self.load_comparison_object(path)
1247            return
1248        
1249        self.dose1 = dose1
1250        self.dose2 = dose2
1251        # axis is taken from the first dose provided
1252        self.voxel_centers = dose1.get_voxel_centers()
1253        self.dose_2_grid_resampled = self.dose2.extract_dose_values_from_coordinates(
1254            self.voxel_centers[2], self.voxel_centers[1], self.voxel_centers[0])
1255        self.percent_difference: BrachyDose = None
1256        self.gamma_index: BrachyDose = None
1257        self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold = gamma_dose_percent_threshold
1258        self.gamma_kwargs = gamma_kwargs
1259        #we can index the dose cutoff to the prescription dose
1260        if(isinstance(prescription_dose, float) or isinstance(prescription_dose, int)):
1261            self.gamma_kwargs["global_normalisation"] = prescription_dose
1262        if(isinstance(max_gamma, float) or isinstance(prescription_dose, int)):
1263            self.max_gamma = max_gamma
1264            self.gamma_kwargs["max_gamma"] = max_gamma
1265        else:
1266            self.max_gamma = 2
1267        # axes values are assumed in cm from the 3ddose formalism
1268        # gamma distance thresholds are usually provided in mm
1269        # pymedphys documentation indicates that the threshold unit must match the axis
1270        # despite the name of the function input containing 'mm'
1271        self.gamma_distance_threshold = gamma_distance_threshold_mm / 10.0
1272        if (compute_percent_difference):
1273            self.compute_percent_difference()
1274        if (compute_gamma_index):
1275            self.compute_gamma_index()
1276
1277    def plot_2d_dose_comparison(self, axis_1_coords: np.ndarray, axis_2_coords: np.ndarray, plane_coord: float, plane: str, plot_titles: tuple):
1278        import itertools
1279        import matplotlib
1280        from matplotlib.ticker import (MultipleLocator, FormatStrFormatter, AutoMinorLocator)
1281        matplotlib.rcParams.update({'font.size': 16})
1282        dose_1_profile = self.dose1.extract_profile_2d(
1283            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1284        dose_2_profile = self.dose2.extract_profile_2d(
1285            axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1286        if (self.percent_difference is not None):
1287            percent_difference_profile = self.percent_difference.extract_profile_2d(
1288                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1289        if (self.gamma_index is not None):
1290            gamma_index_profile = self.gamma_index.extract_profile_2d(
1291                axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, plane_coord, plane)
1292        else:
1293            raise NotImplementedError("""Plotting of a comparison without computing the percent difference or
1294            gamma index is not supported""")
1295        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 10), nrows=2, ncols=2, sharex=True, sharey=True)
1296        plt.tight_layout()
1297        c00 = ax[0, 0].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, dose_1_profile, vmin=0,
1298                              vmax=30, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1299        ax[0, 0].set_title(plot_titles[0], fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1300        cbar00 = fig.colorbar(c00, ax=ax[0, 0])
1301        cbar00.set_label(label='Dose [Gy]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1302        # cbar00.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)
1303        ax[0, 0].invert_yaxis()
1304        ax[0, 0].set_ylabel('y (cm)', fontsize=18)
1305        c01 = ax[0, 1].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, dose_2_profile, vmin=0,
1306                              vmax=30, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1307        ax[0, 1].set_title(plot_titles[1], fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1308        cbar01 = fig.colorbar(c01, ax=ax[0, 1])
1309        cbar01.set_label(label='Dose [Gy]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1310        # cbar01.mappable.set_clim(0, max_dose)
1311        ax[0, 1].invert_yaxis()
1312        c10 = ax[1, 0].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, percent_difference_profile,
1313                              vmin=0, vmax=200, cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1314        ax[1, 0].set_title('Percent Difference', fontsize=20, pad=5, fontweight="bold")
1315        cbar10 = fig.colorbar(c10, ax=ax[1, 0])
1316        cbar10.set_label(label='[%]', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1317        ax[1, 0].invert_yaxis()
1318        ax[1, 0].set_xlabel('x (cm)', fontsize=18)
1319        ax[1, 0].set_ylabel('y (cm)', fontsize=18)
1320
1321        c11 = ax[1, 1].pcolormesh(axis_1_coords, axis_2_coords, gamma_index_profile, vmin=0,
1322                              vmax=self.max_gamma,  cmap='turbo', rasterized=True, antialiased=True)
1323        ax[1, 1].set_title(
1324            f"Gamma ({self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold}% / {int(10.*self.gamma_distance_threshold)} mm)", fontsize=20, pad=5, 
1325            fontweight="bold")
1326        #: Pass Rate = {np.round(self.gamma_pass_ratio*100,1)}%"
1327        cbar11 = fig.colorbar(c11, ax=ax[1, 1])
1328        cbar11.set_label(label='Gamma', size=18, labelpad = 10)
1329        ax[1, 1].invert_yaxis()
1330        ax[1, 1].set_xlabel('x (cm)', fontsize=18)
1331        plt.show()
1332
1333    def compute_percent_difference(self):
1334        self.percent_difference = BrachyDose()
1335        self.percent_difference.grid = np.abs(
1336            self.dose1.grid - self.dose_2_grid_resampled) / self.dose1.grid * 100
1337        self.percent_difference.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1338        self.percent_difference.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1339        self.percent_difference.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1340        self.percent_difference.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1341        self.percent_difference.create_interpolation_function()
1342
1343    def compute_gamma_index(self):
1344        print("Computing gamma index may take time")
1345        logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.DEBUG)
1346        self.gamma_index = BrachyDose()
1347        gamma_index_grid = pymedphys.gamma(tuple(self.voxel_centers), self.dose1.grid, tuple(
1348            self.voxel_centers), self.dose_2_grid_resampled, self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold, self.gamma_distance_threshold,
1349            **self.gamma_kwargs)
1350        #cast the NaNs to 0s
1351        number_excluded = np.sum(np.isnan(gamma_index_grid))
1352        gamma_index_grid[np.isnan(gamma_index_grid)] = -1
1353        self.gamma_index.grid = gamma_index_grid
1354        self.gamma_index.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1355        self.gamma_index.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1356        self.gamma_index.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1357        self.gamma_index.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1358        self.gamma_pass_ratio = (np.sum(self.gamma_index.grid <= 1) - number_excluded) / (self.gamma_index.grid.size - number_excluded)
1359        self.gamma_index.create_interpolation_function()
1360
1361    def save_comparison_object(self, path:str = None):
1362        r"""
1363        Saves the dose comparison object to a file using the pickle module.
1364
1365        Returns:
1366        None
1367        """
1368        if not isinstance(path, str):
1369            root = tk.Tk()
1370            root.withdraw()    
1371            f = fd.asksaveasfile(mode='wb',
1372            defaultextension=".comp", initialdir=os.getcwd(),
1373            title='Save dose comparison object', confirmoverwrite=True)
1374            pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
1375            root.destroy()
1376            f.close()
1377        else: 
1378            with open(path, 'wb') as f:
1379                pickle.dump(self, f, pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL)
1380
1381
1382    def load_comparison_object(self, path:str = None):
1383        r"""
1384        Opens the dose comparison object file and updates the current object's attributes with the loaded object's attributes.
1385
1386        Returns:
1387        None
1388        """
1389        if not isinstance(path, str):
1390            root = tk.Tk()
1391            root.withdraw()
1392            f = fd.askopenfile(mode='rb',
1393            parent=root, initialdir="$HOME", title='Select saved dose comparison file')
1394            self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)
1395                #print(calibration_object_file_path)
1396            root.destroy()
1397            f.close()
1398        else:
1399            with open(path, 'rb') as f:
1400                self.__dict__.update(pickle.load(f).__dict__)

1334        self.percent_difference = BrachyDose()
1335        self.percent_difference.grid = np.abs(
1336            self.dose1.grid - self.dose_2_grid_resampled) / self.dose1.grid * 100
1337        self.percent_difference.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1338        self.percent_difference.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1339        self.percent_difference.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1340        self.percent_difference.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1341        self.percent_difference.create_interpolation_function()
def compute_gamma_index(self): 
1343    def compute_gamma_index(self):
1344        print("Computing gamma index may take time")
1345        logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.DEBUG)
1346        self.gamma_index = BrachyDose()
1347        gamma_index_grid = pymedphys.gamma(tuple(self.voxel_centers), self.dose1.grid, tuple(
1348            self.voxel_centers), self.dose_2_grid_resampled, self.gamma_dose_percent_threshold, self.gamma_distance_threshold,
1349            **self.gamma_kwargs)
1350        #cast the NaNs to 0s
1351        number_excluded = np.sum(np.isnan(gamma_index_grid))
1352        gamma_index_grid[np.isnan(gamma_index_grid)] = -1
1353        self.gamma_index.grid = gamma_index_grid
1354        self.gamma_index.voxel_edges = self.dose1.voxel_edges
1355        self.gamma_index.voxel_size = self.dose1.voxel_size
1356        self.gamma_index.origin_coordinates = self.dose1.origin_coordinates
1357        self.gamma_index.num_voxels = self.dose1.num_voxels
1358        self.gamma_pass_ratio = (np.sum(self.gamma_index.grid <= 1) - number_excluded) / (self.gamma_index.grid.size - number_excluded)
1359        self.gamma_index.create_interpolation_function()
